ldn229Iy07.one_liner: Replaces Euclidean distances in the contrastive RL objective with hyperbolic geodesic distances to match maze route geometry.
ldn229Iy07.problem: In complex navigation environments route distance deviates from Euclidean distance, so contrastive RL critics need great Euclidean depth and wall-clock time scales linearly with depth.
ldn229Iy07.method: Hyperbolic CRL replaces Euclidean distances in CRL's contrastive objective with geodesic distances in hyperbolic space, with curvature swept per environment (per reviews).
ldn229Iy07.key_idea: Embed state-goal representations in hyperbolic space so geodesic distance in the contrastive critic can reflect increasingly tree-like route distances in mazes.
ldn229Iy07.evidence: Goal-reaching tasks spanning locomotion, navigation, and manipulation in online and offline settings, with 10 seeds and bootstrap confidence intervals per reviews; the 512/1024-layer Euclidean curves come from prior work.
ldn229Iy07.claimed_gains: Depth 64 hyperbolic agents outperform 1024-layer Euclidean networks while training more than 12x faster and using about 13x fewer parameters.
ldn229Iy07.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree a minimal, intuitive drop-in change to the critic's distance yields large gains on long-horizon navigation across many environments at far lower compute than very deep Euclidean networks.
ldn229Iy07.main_concern: The headline comparison uses 512/1024-layer Euclidean curves taken from prior work under different protocols, with per-task curvature tuning but no matching tuning for baselines.

YyzpHfaFn8.one_liner: Piecewise Few-Spike neurons with time-dependent parameters approximate nonlinear functions with provable error bounds for ANN-to-SNN conversion.
YyzpHfaFn8.problem: Common ANN-to-SNN conversion methods are theoretically poorly understood and limited in representing nonlinear functions and in activation resolution.
YyzpHfaFn8.method: They categorize conversion methods into two paradigms and analyze their mechanics, then propose Piecewise Few-Spike (PWFS) neurons that introduce time-dependent parameter dynamics for nonlinear function approximation without excessive spike counts. PWFS comes with an explicit convergence guarantee and error bounds that trade approximation accuracy against inference latency.
YyzpHfaFn8.key_idea: Split nonlinear approximation into interval selection and within-interval coding using time-dependent neuron parameters, giving error terms that shrink with M^-2 and 2^-K.
YyzpHfaFn8.evidence: Theoretical propositions on existing conversion methods, a convergence theorem with error bounds, and experiments across different architectures and datasets, including Qwen3 (per reviewers).
YyzpHfaFn8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that analyzing existing conversion methods theoretically and then deriving a provable method is a constructive approach, with a solid error-bound analysis and experiments across architectures.
YyzpHfaFn8.main_concern: The text overstates the limits of general FS neurons and does not clearly state the modifications relative to the original FS neuron or how components such as layer norm, attention, and softmax are converted to spiking operations.

LcWx5qZ1Rj.one_liner: MOBench scores model organisms on seven properties, used to compare seven methods for implanting an impulsive behavior.
LcWx5qZ1Rj.problem: The field lacks a systematic science for building and evaluating model organisms, and how different implant methods change their behavior is unclear.
LcWx5qZ1Rj.method: Introduces MOBench, an automated suite testing model organisms for 7 properties (such as generality, robustness, coherence) derived by backchaining from intended use. As a case study, it trains 7 model organisms for impulsiveness through context, activation and weight interventions and evaluates them.
LcWx5qZ1Rj.key_idea: Properties are chosen by backchaining from how a model organism will be used, then each implant method is scored as a property profile instead of one behavioral metric.
LcWx5qZ1Rj.evidence: Case study on an impulsiveness behavior with seven implant methods across three model scales (7B, 14B, 32B), using shared supervision across training objectives and comparison to the base model.
LcWx5qZ1Rj.claimed_gains: Open character training and fine-tuning reach over 95% general behavior expression, DPO over 60%, and OCT is 1.3 x better than SFT for generality with less coherence degradation.
LcWx5qZ1Rj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that replacing a single behavioral metric with a multi-property profile is useful and that the evaluation is diverse and well controlled across methods.
LcWx5qZ1Rj.main_concern: The case study covers only a benign impulsive persona, so rankings may not transfer to safety-critical or covert misaligned behaviors, and some metrics (introspection, activation similarity) lack motivation.

YvYQiTHtb0.one_liner: Federated graph learning that distills client-side LLM text signals into federatively aggregated edge generators to recover semantically meaningful missing links.
YvYQiTHtb0.problem: Fragmented, non-IID local subgraphs make parameter-aggregation methods unable to capture transferable semantic connection patterns for recovering missing links.
YvYQiTHtb0.method: Each client uses an LLM module on node texts to supervise a local edge generator; the server aggregates generator parameters into a global generator that each client applies within its own node set. A dual-branch GNN decouples personalized local-pattern and shared global-pattern graph representations.
YvYQiTHtb0.key_idea: Share reusable connection functions (edge generators supervised by LLM semantic and pairwise-consistency signals) across clients instead of node relations or representations.
YvYQiTHtb0.evidence: Five benchmark datasets with different numbers of clients, with ablations and baselines such as FedEgo and DFGL2GS named in reviews.
YvYQiTHtb0.claimed_gains: Improved node classification without sharing raw graph data; no numbers stated in the visible abstract.
YvYQiTHtb0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is well organized and that shifting collaboration to reusable edge generators with LLM-derived supervision is a sensible way to share semantics without exchanging raw graph data.
YvYQiTHtb0.main_concern: Contribution is not isolated: gains may come from added LLM features rather than federated edge-generator aggregation, ablations lack a matched dual-branch control, and edges are added only within a client.

P1JbRNZHuA.one_liner: SpecOSS initializes the frequency grid of oscillatory state-space models in closed form from Sturm-Liouville or function-approximation spectra.
P1JbRNZHuA.problem: Oscillatory state-space layers initialize and learn their frequency grid from a random start, although that grid determines which timescales the layer can remember.
P1JbRNZHuA.method: SpecOSS generates the frequency ladder offline from the Sturm-Liouville spectrum of an orthogonal-polynomial family or from an online function-approximation memory operator, and uses it to initialize the diagonal state matrix, which may be trained further or kept fixed.
P1JbRNZHuA.key_idea: Set each oscillator's squared frequency from a closed-form spectral ladder (Sturm-Liouville eigenvalues or memory-operator spectrum) instead of random initialization.
P1JbRNZHuA.evidence: Time-series experiments including PPG-DaLiA, WTH, Motor and SCP1 against LinOSS, plus propositions on when the second-order reduction is exact and on spectral flooring and normalization.
P1JbRNZHuA.claimed_gains: not stated; the truncated abstract says only that even a fixed grid gives strong results on accuracy and error metrics.
P1JbRNZHuA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find drawing the oscillator spectrum from classical spectral theory natural and the theory sound, note large gains on PPG-DaLiA and WTH, and appreciate that the change adds no recurrence cost.
P1JbRNZHuA.main_concern: Evidence is incomplete: standard long-range benchmarks (LRA, EigenWorms) are missing and several variants do not clearly beat random LinOSS initialization (Motor, SCP1), while the architectural change over LinOSS is small.

fuw4wVRBwQ.one_liner: Trains one conditioned actor-critic on groups of parallel environments with different target entropies and discount factors.
fuw4wVRBwQ.problem: Off-policy RL recipes on massively parallel simulators optimize actor and critic under a single training objective whose hyperparameters must be tuned per task or benchmark suite.
fuw4wVRBwQ.method: Parallel environments are partitioned into groups, each with its own target entropy and discount factor; all groups share one actor and critic conditioned on those two values, and each group trains on data collected by all groups. One fixed hyperparameter set and the same group's policy are deployed on every task.
fuw4wVRBwQ.key_idea: Condition a shared actor-critic on per-group target entropy and discount factor and train every group on pooled replay data from all groups.
fuw4wVRBwQ.evidence: 56 continuous-control tasks from four benchmark suites against off-policy baselines including FastTD3 and FlashSAC, with five seeds and ablations.
fuw4wVRBwQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical validation is broad (56 tasks across several suites) with consistent gains over recent baselines at minimal wall-clock overhead, and that the method is practical and easy to implement.
fuw4wVRBwQ.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the conditioned policy, heterogeneous population, shared replay, and cross-mixture relabeling are largely established components combined together.

RvGmPvo58R.one_liner: Modular toolbox replaying measured turbulent plume recordings as RL environments for olfactory source-search benchmarking.
RvGmPvo58R.problem: Learning olfactory navigation needs environments that combine realistic chemical structure with repeatable evaluation, which simulators struggle to provide.
RvGmPvo58R.method: OSRL turns experimentally measured turbulent concentration fields into interactive environments, separating plume replay, sensing, observation processing, and control so one component can be swapped while the rest stay fixed, and supplies a reference track with shared episodes, success geometry, and episode-level records.
RvGmPvo58R.key_idea: Replay measured plume recordings behind a modular sensing, observation, and control interface so controllers or sensor models are compared under fixed shared episodes.
RvGmPvo58R.evidence: Reference-track comparison of a gas-blind control, reactive heuristics, tabular Q-learning, model-based planners, and recurrent PPO with and without an engineered source belief, with transfer to recordings from an independent campaign and a physical gas-sensing robot test.
RvGmPvo58R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the modular, reusable benchmark built on measured plume data, with released code and real-robot validation, addresses a relevant problem.
RvGmPvo58R.main_concern: The benchmark rests on few recordings (six for training, three for testing) and a small physical validation, which limits claims of generalization.

QgbGhfwd3u.one_liner: Rotating values and head outputs with RoPE (QKVO-RoPE) turns attention heads into distance filters, aiding long-context retrieval
QgbGhfwd3u.problem: Standard RoPE rotates queries and keys but leaves values unchanged, and the paper studies what happens when values and head outputs are also rotated.
QgbGhfwd3u.method: Rotates the values and rotates the head output back by the position of the query (QKVO-RoPE). The analysis shows each head becomes a filter over distance: content read from a single position passes through with a phase recording its distance, while content averaged over many positions partly cancels.
QgbGhfwd3u.key_idea: Rotate values by key position and the output back by query position, so single-position reads keep a distance-coded phase while averages over many positions cancel.
QgbGhfwd3u.evidence: Matched Transformer pairs from 130M to 1.3B parameters tested on needle retrieval and perplexity beyond the training length, with head-level frequency analysis and ablations over rotation combinations.
QgbGhfwd3u.claimed_gains: Beyond the training length, value-rotated models retrieve needles that their unrotated counterparts miss entirely, and up to 760M parameters they extrapolate with lower perplexity.
QgbGhfwd3u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean matched-pair experiments, the analysis of rotated values cancelling in diffuse contexts, and the honest reporting of negative results and failed predictions.
QgbGhfwd3u.main_concern: The retrieval and extrapolation evidence is limited (repeated-passage backgrounds, unequal baseline budgets, no matched NTK-scaled retrieval controls), so the advantage over other positional methods is unclear.

WGz5ryPa7P.one_liner: Warps the inputs and outputs of a frozen single-object skill so it handles many objects.
WGz5ryPa7P.problem: RL manipulation policies degrade when the object count exceeds the training range, a covariate shift that also changes the state dimension.
WGz5ryPa7P.method: A selection policy picks the next object, and a warping policy reads a fixed-size local view around it and emits a multiplier and offset for every quantity the skill reads and every action it outputs. The skill runs as a black box under this affine warp, and both policies are trained with PPO on the multi-object reward.
WGz5ryPa7P.key_idea: Apply per-quantity affine multipliers and offsets to a frozen skill's observations and actions, computed from a local view whose size is independent of object count.
WGz5ryPa7P.evidence: Cube arrangement tasks with a gantry robot and a Franka Panda arm, plus a probability analysis of placing all N objects within a skill-invocation budget linear in N; reviews also mention a real-world setting.
WGz5ryPa7P.claimed_gains: A policy trained on at most nine objects generalizes zero-shot to up to thirty, five times the largest count with a published learned result (TL;DR).
WGz5ryPa7P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clear problem, the simple frozen-skill warping design, and strong object-count extrapolation against tuned baselines.
WGz5ryPa7P.main_concern: The success metric is defined inconsistently between Section 4 and Appendix C, and generalization to other object sizes or types and failure modes (e.g., knocked-down cubes) is not analyzed.

7oN5Rjf8vo.one_liner: Controlled framework measuring how system-level and skill-level privacy guidance changes which information sources LLM agents choose.
7oN5Rjf8vo.problem: Prior work documents agent privacy failures, but it is unclear how the presentation of privacy guidance influences an agent's choice among public, confidential or user-supplied information sources.
7oN5Rjf8vo.method: PrivacySkills has 55 synthetic tasks across 11 personal-information categories with 169 skills describing acquisition pathways. Privacy guidance is given through system instructions, skill-level metadata labels, or both, while user availability and urgency framing are varied.
7oN5Rjf8vo.key_idea: Hold task-relevant value constant across public, confidential and user-interaction pathways and vary only how privacy guidance is presented, at system level versus skill level.
7oN5Rjf8vo.evidence: Five open-weight models on 55 synthetic tasks with counterbalanced tool presentation order.
7oN5Rjf8vo.claimed_gains: With users available and no guidance, agents access confidential sources in 30% of valid runs, rising to 45% when users are unavailable; skill-level intrusiveness labels give a modest reduction (24% on average) and combining them with system instructions roughly halves confidential access.
7oN5Rjf8vo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled, counterbalanced design and the focus on how agents acquire information, with categories grounded in real privacy legislation.
7oN5Rjf8vo.main_concern: The benchmark has limited diversity (every task shares a three-source structure with one missing attribute) and omits task-completion and appropriateness analysis.

cAzlFf5N6n.one_liner: Certificate transport avoids accurate inner solves in min-max problems with a low-dimensional block by reusing a lower model across slices.
cAzlFf5N6n.problem: Nested min-max schemes over a few adversarial or dual variables solve each inner problem accurately, costing a multiplicative m*sqrt(kappa) factor in oracle calls for x.
cAzlFf5N6n.method: Certificate transport keeps a strongly convex lower model of one slice f(.,y) and uses it to warm-start a short accelerated run on the next slice. Each y-oracle call either cuts the localizer or, by concavity in y, transports the model to a mixture of two slices with a certified increase.
cAzlFf5N6n.key_idea: Keep a strongly convex lower model of one slice and, by concavity in y, transport it to the next slice to warm-start a short accelerated run.
cAzlFf5N6n.evidence: Oracle-complexity theory, with experiments using certified accuracy targets and nested and level-method baselines, including Group DRO per reviews.
cAzlFf5N6n.claimed_gains: For m=1, an epsilon-saddle point with O(sqrt(kappa)log(1/epsilon)) x-oracle calls and O(log(1/epsilon)) y-oracle calls, optimal in y calls and total calls, versus O(m*sqrt(kappa)*log^2(1/epsilon)) x-oracle calls for the standard nested approach.
cAzlFf5N6n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing partial primal progress while keeping a valid certificate avoids accurate inner solves and gives strong oracle-complexity bounds supported by experiments.
cAzlFf5N6n.main_concern: Practical runtime benefit is unresolved: only oracle calls are compared, not wall-clock time, and the center-computation overhead can become substantial as the low-dimensional block grows.

pfC0aJYJML.one_liner: Proves adaptive adversaries cost a Theta(log k) factor in bandit multiclass classification, with matching finite-class separations.
pfC0aJYJML.problem: The concept-class adaptivity problem posed at NeurIPS 2024 asks how much more an adaptive adversary can cost a learner than an oblivious one in bandit multiclass classification.
pfC0aJYJML.method: Combines two costs certified by oblivious adversaries into a potential whose decrease pays for adaptive mistakes (upper bound), and builds finite classes that assign different continuation budgets to parts of a class while reusing one label alphabet across a finite recursion (lower bound).
pfC0aJYJML.key_idea: A potential built from two oblivious-adversary costs pays for adaptive mistakes in the upper bound, while recursive class constructions with varying continuation budgets give the matching lower bound.
pfC0aJYJML.evidence: Proofs of a logarithmic comparison for every concept class including infinite ones, a finite-class lower bound, a four-function minimal witness, 5/4 tower asymptotics, and composition bounds.
pfC0aJYJML.claimed_gains: The worst-case ratio lies between (2/3 - o(1)) ln k and (1 + o(1)) ln k, with a sharp 5/4 limiting ratio for the tower family.
pfC0aJYJML.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a precise answer to the existence question, with a four-function minimal witness, exact finite-class separations, and a meaningful distinction between concept and pattern classes.
pfC0aJYJML.main_concern: Reviewers find the central quantitative question only partly resolved, since the demonstrated gaps are constant-factor and some bounds are loose, and the presentation is dense.

PhFsCUUCn6.one_liner: Goodness-of-fit test for temporal point processes on aggregated counts, using simulated or particle-filter forecasts and Monte Carlo-calibrated signed residuals.
PhFsCUUCn6.problem: Exact-time diagnostics such as time rescaling must impute event times for count-only records, and for history-dependent models the chosen imputation can determine the test result.
PhFsCUUCn6.method: ObsCritic criticizes a model through the distribution it induces on recorded counts, estimating count forecasts by simulation or particle filtering and accumulating signed residuals that show which counts are mispredicted after which histories, with Monte Carlo calibration of the whole procedure.
PhFsCUUCn6.key_idea: Test the observed counts through forecast distributions conditioned on recorded histories, calibrating the whole procedure by Monte Carlo, instead of imputing event times.
PhFsCUUCn6.evidence: Synthetic data with fixed count frequencies and transitions, a Transformer Hawkes Process misspecification test, and real datasets (abstract truncated).
PhFsCUUCn6.claimed_gains: Even when the model is correct, time rescaling rejects 4% of records with uniform imputation and 100% with skewed imputation, while ObsCritic detects higher-order dynamics changes that imputation-based tests miss.
PhFsCUUCn6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the central idea of testing the observed record rather than an imputation simple and convincing, with Monte Carlo calibration giving valid finite-sample inference.
PhFsCUUCn6.main_concern: Power depends on the test features aligning with the alternative, with the headline result resting on one construction, and scalability of particle filtering to long or multivariate processes is unclear.

bh3AbXUIFd.one_liner: Shows strong tau-abstraction need not imply constructivity, and characterizes constructivity via preservation of intervention composition.
bh3AbXUIFd.problem: Beckers and Halpern conjectured that strong tau-abstraction implies constructive abstraction under minor conditions, but positive results existed only for linear structural causal models with extra assumptions.
bh3AbXUIFd.method: The paper shows a fixed edgeless low-level model admits strong abstractions with arbitrary high-level DAGs, and proves that preservation of intervention composition on the full canonical domain suffices for constructivity. On restricted low-level domains with full high-level intervention coverage, composition preservation is equivalent to constructivity.
bh3AbXUIFd.key_idea: Constructivity of a strong tau-abstraction is characterized by whether the low-to-high intervention map preserves composition of interventions on a suitably restricted low-level domain.
bh3AbXUIFd.evidence: Theoretical proofs plus a controlled nonlinear learning experiment in which composition constraints improve prediction over unregularized learning when input correlations change.
bh3AbXUIFd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the results are rigorous and address an open conjecture, showing strong abstraction is weaker than constructive abstraction and characterizing the gap through intervention-composition preservation.
bh3AbXUIFd.main_concern: Significance and construction: the counterexample may rely on cancellations that the linear-case assumptions aimed to exclude, and the practical importance of the characterization is questioned.

fA61Xw7Ii7.one_liner: Replaces MLP lifting in neural operators with learnable Gabor filters and processes a learned latent with discrete wavelet transforms.
fA61Xw7Ii7.problem: Neural-operator lifting is almost always a generic MLP, and scale-decomposing kernels need regular grids while point-cloud and mesh kernels lack explicit multi-scale bias.
fA61Xw7Ii7.method: GLoW replaces the MLP lifting with a fully learnable Gabor filter in which each lifted channel is an oscillatory feature modulated by a learned spatial window. Lifted features are aggregated into a learned latent space where a discrete wavelet transform decomposes the representation across scales (abstract truncated).
fA61Xw7Ii7.key_idea: Gabor-filter lifting gives windowed oscillatory channels, and a wavelet transform with band mixing in a learned latent space gives scale-separated processing on irregular geometries.
fA61Xw7Ii7.evidence: Six standard PDE benchmarks and three aerodynamic datasets with different geometries, including AirfRANS extrapolation beyond the training range, plus ablations (from reviews).
fA61Xw7Ii7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that targeting the overlooked lifting stage is well motivated and that coverage across PDE and aerodynamic benchmarks is broad.
fA61Xw7Ii7.main_concern: The method is seen as an incremental combination of Gabor filters and a wavelet module replacing Transolver attention, and the ablations do not isolate where the gain comes from.

ZIzH3a7ywS.one_liner: Derives RL rewards for generative reward models from relative preference rankings (self-competitive and anchor-guided) instead of scalar scores.
ZIzH3a7ywS.problem: Generative reward models rank responses well but do not yield effective RL signals because their comparative nature mismatches the scalar scoring paradigm of existing RL algorithms.
ZIzH3a7ywS.method: RRC builds rewards from preference rankings using self-competitive ranking, which compares sampled responses, and anchor-guided ranking, which compares against a small set of reference responses. It acts at reward-computation time and plugs into GRPO without retraining the reward model.
ZIzH3a7ywS.key_idea: Turn pairwise judgments from a generative reward model into rewards by counting wins among sampled responses or against reference anchors rather than reading a scalar score.
ZIzH3a7ywS.evidence: Open-ended chat and reasoning benchmarks such as AlpacaEval2 and ArenaHardV2, across two policy models, compared with existing reward-construction approaches.
ZIzH3a7ywS.claimed_gains: Examples of gains over existing reward construction are 35.8% to 41.3% on AlpacaEval2 and 8.0% to 11.2% on ArenaHardV2.
ZIzH3a7ywS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a real mismatch between ranking-strong generative reward models and scalar RL rewards, and that the plug-and-play method gives consistent gains with clear writing.
ZIzH3a7ywS.main_concern: Novelty and claims are not isolated: components resemble tournament and anchor-based ranking, no control applies rank-based construction to a discriminative reward model, and margin-awareness is not established.

gL4S2LvCwX.one_liner: Mesh-restricted GENERIC construction guarantees skew-adjoint, PSD, and energy-entropy-degenerate updates for any neural readout in graph simulators.
gL4S2LvCwX.problem: Trajectory accuracy does not show whether an executed update of a graph neural simulator is admissible under GENERIC's reversible-dissipative algebra on a mesh with a prescribed metric, admissible directions, and boundary ports.
gL4S2LvCwX.method: The paper defines Mesh-GENERIC Compatibility and derives a sufficient construction. MAGNS implements it through neural dynamical assembly that maps learned constitutive quantities and operator coefficients into compatible dynamics before integration.
gL4S2LvCwX.key_idea: Assemble operators directly within the intersection of mesh-admissible directions and the GENERIC-compatible cone so the algebraic conditions hold for every readout, independent of training.
gL4S2LvCwX.evidence: Long-horizon acoustics, coupled thermoelastic and electromagnetic systems, and fixed-weight Darcy interventions, with controlled interventions on integration, boundary exchange, operator assembly, and Hodge-space admissibility.
gL4S2LvCwX.claimed_gains: On long-horizon acoustics, MAGNS reduces mean rollout MSE by 28% on validation and 14% on test relative to the strongest structured baseline.
gL4S2LvCwX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the construction gives a clean, constructive guarantee of GENERIC conditions on meshes and is tested on diverse dynamics.
gL4S2LvCwX.main_concern: The empirical benefit of the strict compatibility constraints is small and not isolated: free-operator ablation differences are tiny, many results use single seeds, and no experiment jointly stresses geometric restriction and reversible-dissipative coupling.

PVdVWTVx5f.one_liner: Re-encoding an image through another model's autoencoder spoofs latent-diffusion attribution; READ recovers the source from denoiser responses.
PVdVWTVx5f.problem: Reconstruction-error attribution is ambiguous because distinct Stable Diffusion models sharing an autoencoder give identical errors, and it can be redirected after generation.
PVdVWTVx5f.method: CMR passes an image from model M1 once through attack model M2's encoder and decoder to induce false attribution to M2, without diffusion sampling or attribution queries. READ learns attribution from several denoisers' relative responses to controlled latent perturbations, calibrated on clean images.
PVdVWTVx5f.key_idea: Re-encoding with another model's autoencoder plants that model's reconstruction signature, while differing denoisers' responses to latent perturbations still reveal the true source.
PVdVWTVx5f.evidence: Twelve generative models, attacks on AEDR, AEROBLADE, and LatentTracer, plus JPEG and blur controls, adaptive attacks, and extra baselines (from reviews).
PVdVWTVx5f.claimed_gains: CMR raises mean attack-model acceptance to 93.5-99.8% for AEDR, AEROBLADE, and LatentTracer across 12 generative models; the READ result figure is cut off in the abstract.
PVdVWTVx5f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree CMR is a simple, effective attack exposing a real limit of reconstruction-based attribution, and that READ is a simple, interpretable defense backed by extensive experiments.
PVdVWTVx5f.main_concern: READ's gain is not isolated from its stronger supervision and model access (seven observer models, 500 labeled clean images per source), baseline comparisons mix datasets and protocols, and READ often rejects rather than recovers.

3vkzqldlUw.one_liner: Shows Coconut-style continuous CoT reads earlier KV-cache entries at answer readout, with a frontier-history Transformer construction for graph reachability.
3vkzqldlUw.problem: It is unclear how continuous chain-of-thought, which feeds hidden states back while keeping a persistent KV history, uses past information to support reasoning.
3vkzqldlUw.method: Interventions restrict or restore latent-history access in Coconut during generation and at readout. A frontier-history model for graph reachability shows a two-block Transformer can do exact frontier updates by superposing the current frontier in feedback and keeping earlier frontiers in the KV cache, and a trained two-layer Coconut model is analyzed.
3vkzqldlUw.key_idea: The current frontier is superposed in the fed-back latent while earlier frontiers persist in the KV cache and are read out at the answer.
3vkzqldlUw.evidence: Cache-restriction and restoration interventions on Coconut, a constructive two-block Transformer for graph reachability, and paired interventions on a trained two-layer model (a six-layer checkpoint in the appendix).
3vkzqldlUw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the controlled interventions and the formal construction together show that earlier latent KV entries matter for continuous reasoning.
3vkzqldlUw.main_concern: Takeaways are limited and theory is only partly matched to trained models: past KV mattering is expected for Transformers, and the construction needs N continuous tokens versus graph diameter in prior theory on the same task.

G9iLDC17r6.one_liner: Low-rank RNN whose trial-specific static input biases act as bifurcation parameters, inferring control parameters from single-trial neural activity.
G9iLDC17r6.problem: Standard models treat trial-to-trial variability as noise around a fixed system or as discrete regime switches, missing how continuous internal states such as arousal gradually deform a circuit's flow field.
G9iLDC17r6.method: A low-rank recurrent network is fit per trial, with constant trial-specific input biases that deform the flow field without driving activity over time. It is validated in a teacher-student setting, applied to mouse and monkey motor cortex, and extended to a generative model.
G9iLDC17r6.key_idea: Reframe single-trial fitting as inferring low-dimensional control parameters: constant per-trial input biases to a shared low-rank RNN act as bifurcation parameters that reshape its flow field.
G9iLDC17r6.evidence: Teacher-student recovery of ground-truth dynamics and bifurcation structure, mouse and monkey motor cortex recordings, and partial transfer across sessions and subjects.
G9iLDC17r6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the model is well motivated, interpretable, analyzable with low-rank theory, and evaluated on several datasets and species.
G9iLDC17r6.main_concern: Related changing-dynamics models (dLDS, p-dLDS, LFADS-style) are not compared, and the many-flow-fields claim is shown only in simulation, with no fixed-point or bifurcation analysis on real data.

d9vd3EavkN.one_liner: RL-trains a 20B search subagent inside a stateful harness that keeps working memory, evidence links, and verification records.
d9vd3EavkN.problem: Training search agents as policies over growing transcripts forces RL to optimize both semantic search decisions and recoverable bookkeeping that the environment could maintain more reliably.
d9vd3EavkN.method: Harness-1 is a 20B retrieval subagent trained with RL inside a harness holding a candidate pool, an importance-tagged curated set, evidence links, verification records, deduplicated observations, and budget-aware context rendering. The policy keeps the semantic decisions: what to search, keep or discard, verify, and when to stop.
d9vd3EavkN.key_idea: Move routine state management (candidate pool, evidence links, verification records, context rendering) into the environment so RL optimizes only semantic search decisions.
d9vd3EavkN.evidence: Eight retrieval benchmarks spanning web, finance, patents, and multi-hop QA, with component ablations and a harness-swap experiment, compared with Context-1 and Tongyi DeepResearch (from reviews).
d9vd3EavkN.claimed_gains: Reaches 0.730 average curated recall across eight retrieval benchmarks, outperforming the next strongest open search subagent by +11.4 points.
d9vd3EavkN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the harness design is clear and practical and that the 20B agent gives strong, cost-efficient recall across eight benchmarks, including held-out transfer.
d9vd3EavkN.main_concern: The benefit of stateful offloading during training is not isolated: component ablations remove harness parts only at inference time, and no run trains the same recipe in a thin harness.

6i1BvIkyZI.one_liner: Benchmark pairing map-view correspondence tests (scale, pose, identity) with navigation from the same pose for multimodal models.
6i1BvIkyZI.problem: General models' ability to relate an allocentric map to their egocentric view has received little systematic study, because maps are judged only by the navigation of the system they were built for.
6i1BvIkyZI.method: BEARING has 5 task categories and 9 tasks sharing 60 routes in 9 Matterport3D buildings, from closed-loop navigation to open-loop segment planning and static questions at segment starts. It evaluates 9 closed-source, open-source, and embodied models against a human reference.
6i1BvIkyZI.key_idea: Test scale, pose, and identity correspondences at the same physical poses where navigation uses them, so static skill scores can be checked against local planning and route progress.
6i1BvIkyZI.evidence: Evaluation of 9 models with map-format comparisons and interventions on the compass, scale bar, and agent marker, plus correlation of identity tests with segment progress.
6i1BvIkyZI.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports that all 9 evaluated models remain well below a human reference, with the widest gap in self-localisation.
6i1BvIkyZI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark targets a meaningful gap by tying map-view correspondence to navigation at shared states and goes beyond aggregate scores with interventions.
6i1BvIkyZI.main_concern: Scale and external validity are limited: only 9 Matterport3D buildings, 60 routes, and one map style, shared poses reduce independent samples, and each model is essentially run once.

jIANaR1p68.one_liner: Compresses 3D Gaussian Splatting with anchor-wise causal context without spatial aggregation and integer inference for cross-platform decoding.
jIANaR1p68.problem: Spatial context modeling over irregular 3DGS representations complicates training and coding, and floating-point context inference causes numerical inconsistencies that break entropy decoding across platforms.
jIANaR1p68.method: COSA-GS derives geometry context from each anchor's coordinates to model a compact learnable anchor latent, fuses the two into an anchor context for attribute coding, and uses only linear layers and activations. It trains with rate-distortion optimization and adaptive Gaussian pruning, plus quantization-aware training and integer inference.
jIANaR1p68.key_idea: Code each anchor's attributes from its own coordinate-derived context and a learnable latent, with no neighbor gathering, using an integer-quantized context network for bit-exact decoding.
jIANaR1p68.evidence: Compression experiments (datasets not visible in the truncated abstract); reviews mention a cross-platform test on the quantization-aware variant and decoding-speed comparisons with HAC++ and PCGS.
jIANaR1p68.claimed_gains: The abstract gives no figures; a review reports decoding in about 0.13 s versus about 25 s for HAC++ and PCGS with a lower bitrate.
jIANaR1p68.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the context model is simple, fully parallel, and fast to decode, and that it addresses practical issues (coding speed, cross-platform consistency) rarely studied.
jIANaR1p68.main_concern: The premise is not validated and novelty is limited: the per-anchor latent resembles a ContextGS hyperprior, the geometry-context ablation changes little, and cross-platform tests lack a floating-point baseline.

gByqYqWU6U.one_liner: Embeds a CLIP-derived 32-bit facial content code in non-facial regions with geometry-aligned recovery to verify face integrity.
gByqYqWU6U.problem: Facial integrity verification needs an embedded signal that represents the original face and survives processing, but random payloads give no content reference and geometric transformations break the correspondence localized watermarking relies on.
gByqYqWU6U.method: A compact semantic reference is derived from the protected face by projecting frozen CLIP features with PCA and binarizing to 32 bits, combined with a 16-bit tracing field, and embedded only in the surrounding region so facial pixels are unchanged. A shared geometric estimate aligns watermark recovery and face encoding, and the recovered code is compared with one recomputed from the received face.
gByqYqWU6U.key_idea: A face-derived binary code is watermarked into the surrounding region, and one shared geometric estimate rectifies both payload recovery and face re-encoding for comparison.
gByqYqWU6U.evidence: Experiments across four settings (truncated in the abstract); reviews mention edits from SimSwap, CSCS, StarGAN, and Stable Diffusion inpainting, FFHQ transfer, and ablations on alignment, reader adaptation, and content representations.
gByqYqWU6U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design keeps protected facial pixels unchanged and that controlled ablations support the empirical conclusions.
gByqYqWU6U.main_concern: Novelty and reliability are limited: components have close precedents (LampMark, RecoverMark, MaskWM-style transport, SyncSeal), samples without a valid score are excluded without a reported rate, and the threat model covers only specified editors.

w0IpAgNFDP.one_liner: Learns L0-gated KV eviction for full-duplex speech models, tuned on an LLM judge's verdicts of generated replies.
w0IpAgNFDP.problem: In full-duplex speech models the KV cache grows with elapsed time even during silence, recency and accumulated attention miss token importance, and next-token loss poorly tracks failures where the model takes the turn but the reply loses content.
w0IpAgNFDP.method: DuplexKV trains a lightweight L0-Gate jointly with the backbone under a fixed cache budget with an L0-regularized objective, combined with attention and recency at inference. Judged Eviction Tuning (JET) then tunes the gate on an LLM judge's verdicts about replies generated under eviction.
w0IpAgNFDP.key_idea: Learn per-token retention with an L0 gate under a hard budget, then tune it on judge verdicts of replies generated under eviction rather than on next-token loss.
w0IpAgNFDP.evidence: Cache-content analysis on MiniCPM-o 4.5 and Raon-SpeechChat, and the user-interruption task of Full-Duplex-Bench on both backbones.
w0IpAgNFDP.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract claims the highest judge score among prior eviction policies on both backbones even at small budgets, with an advantage that grows in longer conversations.
w0IpAgNFDP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis of cache contents by speaker, modality, and control tokens is informative and that the rollout-free training with JET keeps response quality and takeover rates high.
w0IpAgNFDP.main_concern: JET labels and method components are not cleanly validated: one binary judge label per boundary token updates a shared gate despite head specialization, and the value of conditioning on the reply is not isolated.

gxWFjev3td.one_liner: Separates the learning rate where one-step feature learning aligns with the task from the batch size needed to resolve it.
gxWFjev3td.problem: A population gradient can point toward a task-relevant direction even when a finite empirical gradient cannot resolve it, and the two scales are not distinguished.
gxWFjev3td.method: The paper studies one-step feature learning in two-layer networks with spiked Gaussian inputs and defines two target-weighted covariance quantities: population amplification A sets the learning-rate scale for order-one overlap, and H/A^2 gives a sufficient batch scale. It derives a joint critical law at the critical batch scale and an exact alignment-anisotropy map for rank-one spikes.
gxWFjev3td.key_idea: Two target-weighted covariance quantities, A for the onset learning rate and H/A^2 for the batch scale, vary independently, so anisotropy can amplify movement without making it estimable from finite data.
gxWFjev3td.evidence: Theorems under a smooth activation class and triangular conditions, with direct-onset, factorial, and geometry-wide experiments that support the predicted normalizations and show finite-dimensional deviations.
gxWFjev3td.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating the strength of the expected update from the batch size needed to estimate it is a useful question and the joint critical law is interesting.
gxWFjev3td.main_concern: Clarity and prior-work positioning are weak: notation is dense and partly undefined, the introduction is hard to follow, and a NeurIPS 2023 paper by Ba et al. already identifies the same A term.

gj7I78SrN5.one_liner: Proves that transformers with CoT trained on a gradient-descent teacher, then on true weights, learn heavy-ball acceleration for in-context regression.
gj7I78SrN5.problem: Prior theory shows CoT transformers can imitate a gradient-descent teacher for in-context weight prediction, but not whether CoT can go beyond the teacher algorithm.
gj7I78SrN5.method: After initial supervision from a gradient-descent teacher, a second stage supervises the whole trajectory with the true regression weights. The analysis shows the trained transformer then implements the heavy-ball method, accelerating over the teacher.
gj7I78SrN5.key_idea: After gradient-descent-teacher supervision, training CoT steps on the true weights with gradient flow converges to heavy-ball updates, with no heavy-ball teacher.
gj7I78SrN5.evidence: Theoretical analysis of both training stages, including convergence and the learned algorithm, under linear attention, few CoT steps, a sparse initialization, and population gradient flow; reviewers describe the experiments as small.
gj7I78SrN5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the research question is natural, the second stage without teacher forcing is technically non-trivial, and heavy-ball emerging without heavy-ball supervision is interesting.
gj7I78SrN5.main_concern: Assumptions are strong (linear attention, very few CoT steps, frozen block, population gradient flow) and calling the result a discovered algorithm overstates it, since heavy-ball looks like the only optimum of the stage-two objective.

EKOJO3jGHl.one_liner: Adapts Diff-Instruct and trajectory distribution matching to continuous diffusion language models for one- and few-step generation.
EKOJO3jGHl.problem: Image score-distillation recipes do not transfer to continuous diffusion language models because distillation acts on expected token embeddings while generation needs discrete token decisions, so higher confidence can collapse samples onto few tokens.
EKOJO3jGHl.method: The paper argues distillation should resolve token-level uncertainty while preserving noise-dependent variation across samples, guiding generator initialization (a denoiser's conditional mean is not a suitable start) and score modeling of the student's distribution. It adapts Diff-Instruct and trajectory distribution matching on these principles.
EKOJO3jGHl.key_idea: Initialize and score the student so it resolves token-level uncertainty yet keeps noise-dependent variation, instead of reusing the conditional-mean denoiser and image-style objectives.
EKOJO3jGHl.evidence: One-step and few-step generation on LM1B and OpenWebText with two continuous diffusion language models, ablations, and 1-4 step budgets, measured by generative perplexity and unigram entropy (from reviews).
EKOJO3jGHl.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports only that effective one-step and few-step generation is enabled on LM1B and OpenWebText.
EKOJO3jGHl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis of why image distillation fails for categorical-head language models is careful and the resulting components improve one- and few-step results.
EKOJO3jGHl.main_concern: Evaluation and baselines are thin: only generative perplexity and unigram entropy from single runs on 179M-parameter unconditional models, incoherent samples, and unclear necessity over DMD-style methods and prior DLM-One.

CGTftOZFpV.one_liner: Splits agent competence into task and interface competence and uses harness rehearsal to train interface use separately from task knowledge.
CGTftOZFpV.problem: When an LLM agent fails under a given harness, it is unclear whether it lacks task knowledge or the competence to operate the interface, and harness-conditioned training may improve one while degrading the other.
CGTftOZFpV.method: The paper formulates task competence versus interface competence and studies multi-harness distillation and single-harness training on four reasoning and agentic benchmarks. It introduces harness rehearsal to separate interface supervision from task supervision (abstract truncated).
CGTftOZFpV.key_idea: Harness rehearsal supplies interface practice on the target harness separately from cross-harness task supervision, and the two are combined in a 2x2 design.
CGTftOZFpV.evidence: Four reasoning and agentic benchmarks (MedAgentBench, Reasoning Gym, and BFCL multi-turn per reviews) with distillation, supervised finetuning, and RL settings.
CGTftOZFpV.claimed_gains: The abstract gives no figures; a review cites MedAgentBench target-harness success of 2.0% and 9.5% for cross-harness supervision and rehearsal alone versus 34.4% combined.
CGTftOZFpV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the rehearsal experiment poses a clear question and that single-harness distillation can collapse performance on unseen harnesses, which is useful for building agentic SFT data.
CGTftOZFpV.main_concern: The task/interface decomposition is an interpretation rather than an identified mechanism, and the combined arm in the 2x2 is not size-matched, so part of the gain may come from more data.

H3ReHEhtpw.one_liner: Composes residual and product quantization recursively into parallel Semantic IDs, with geometry-aware embedding init and progressive hard-negative training.
H3ReHEhtpw.problem: Product-quantization Semantic IDs allow parallel single-forward prediction but quantize subspaces independently, so they do not capture hierarchical relationships among items.
H3ReHEhtpw.method: Cuber combines RPQ-Tree, a recursive composition of residual and product quantization compatible with single-forward prediction, with a geometry-aware initialization that transfers quantization structure into code-token embeddings. A progressive training mechanism uses partial-tree predictions to mine harder negatives.
H3ReHEhtpw.key_idea: Recursively nest residual and product quantization in a tree to inject hierarchy into Semantic IDs while keeping parallel prediction of codes.
H3ReHEhtpw.evidence: Extensive experiments against competitive baselines in generative recommendation (datasets not visible in the truncated abstract).
H3ReHEhtpw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the trade-off between parallel decoding efficiency and hierarchical item structure is well motivated and RPQ-Tree is a flexible, technically coherent framework.
H3ReHEhtpw.main_concern: Dependencies appear only in offline quantization and embedding initialization because codes are still predicted independently by separate heads, and the components resemble residual product quantization and standard hard-negative mining.

ikKE3epkFV.one_liner: Proves any approximation factor below 3 for comparing two known models in total variation needs Omega(N/log N) samples.
ikKE3epkFV.problem: A classical selector achieves factor 3 with a sample budget independent of the number of outcomes, but how much data a better factor requires was left open, with earlier lower bounds far below the upper bound.
ikKE3epkFV.method: The paper extends the Bousquet-Kane-Moran construction with a moment-matching step: two seed laws become nearby matched laws agreeing on their first Theta(log N) moments, so two random targets rank the candidates oppositely while their samples are hard to distinguish. The bound holds for candidates taking just two probability values.
ikKE3epkFV.key_idea: Moment-match two nearby target laws on their first Theta(log N) moments so samples cannot tell them apart while they rank the two candidates oppositely.
ikKE3epkFV.evidence: Theoretical proofs, with an existing TV estimator supplying the matching upper bound; a reviewer states the proofs were verified.
ikKE3epkFV.claimed_gains: Every fixed approximation factor c in [1,3) requires Omega(N/log N) target samples at sufficiently small fixed additive error, matching an existing TV estimator's upper bound.
ikKE3epkFV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the tight sample-complexity result closing the gap between the earlier Omega(sqrt(N)) lower bound and the upper bound is a nice contribution with correct, interesting moment-matching arguments.
ikKE3epkFV.main_concern: The writing is unclear with undefined quantities and weak positioning against related work such as Aiyer et al., and the result is worst-case only.

2Sogb2iXuW.one_liner: Convergence analysis of FedAvg when clients are sampled uniformly from a window that cyclically advances each round.
2Sogb2iXuW.problem: Existing federated-learning convergence frameworks assume full or uniform sampling, and prior cyclic-participation analyses cover only restricted objectives or specific cyclic patterns.
2Sogb2iXuW.method: Cycwin-FL applies FedAvg with uniform sampling from a window of B among M clients that advances by N_w clients per communication round. The analysis covers Polyak-Lojasiewicz and general smooth non-convex objectives, including the case where gcd(M,N_w) does not divide B.
2Sogb2iXuW.key_idea: When gcd(M,N_w) divides B, window-induced bias cancels across rounds so rates match vanilla FedAvg; otherwise cyclic imbalance prevents convergence to a stationary point.
2Sogb2iXuW.evidence: Convergence theorems for PL and smooth non-convex objectives, plus experiments on multiple datasets with ablations of key system parameters (from reviews).
2Sogb2iXuW.claimed_gains: If gcd(M,N_w) divides B, an O~(T^-1) bound on the optimality gap for PL objectives and the same O(T^-1/2) rate as vanilla FedAvg for smooth non-convex objectives.
2Sogb2iXuW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical analysis is comprehensive, covering PL and non-convex cases with explicit sampling noise, local drift, and cyclic imbalance terms for a relevant availability setting.
2Sogb2iXuW.main_concern: Novelty and practicality are limited: it is essentially FedAvg under a generalized cyclic schedule, the extension of earlier cyclic analyses looks predictable, assumptions and horizon requirements are restrictive, and experiments mostly match FedAvg.

JPHtub1bRd.one_liner: Routes on-policy distillation gradients per parameter block using the gradient of the student's verified past successes as a reference.
JPHtub1bRd.problem: Token-level teacher feedback on student-generated prefixes can push the student away from behavior it already performs correctly, and scalar token reweighting shrinks every parameter component together, discarding the part that agrees with past successes.
JPHtub1bRd.method: PCGR uses the gradient of verified past successes as a reference: the prefix's accumulated teacher-student discrepancy sets how much reference conflict an update may keep, and blockwise reference geometry decides where the rest is removed. This gives a convex problem with a closed-form gate per parameter block.
JPHtub1bRd.key_idea: A closed-form per-parameter-block gate keeps reference-compatible gradient components and removes conflicting ones, with allowed conflict set by the prefix's accumulated teacher-student discrepancy.
JPHtub1bRd.evidence: Four verifiable task families with Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B students, a measurement that 71.2% of OPD token gradients mix compatible and conflicting blocks, and equal-GPU-hour comparisons (from a review).
JPHtub1bRd.claimed_gains: Improves the macro score over OPD by 2.5 and 2.0 points with Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B students, and nearly halves a quantity cut off in the abstract.
JPHtub1bRd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear (homogeneous updates can damage already-learned behavior) and that parameter-level routing with verified reference gradients is a principled idea supported by ablations.
JPHtub1bRd.main_concern: Gains are modest and the method is under-specified: routing criteria and behavior with a wrong reference signal are unclear, sources of improvement are not disentangled, and extra backward passes and reliance on verifiers raise scaling questions.

lDwFVzYN2W.one_liner: Bias-variance theory for when dual query-document projections beat shared ones, with a cross-fitted selector (CARS) choosing from training data.
lDwFVzYN2W.problem: The theoretical basis for choosing between shared and dual query-document projections in dense retrieval is unclear.
lDwFVzYN2W.method: The paper models low-rank bilinear scoring, where shared projections induce positive-semidefinite operators and dual projections realize arbitrary low-rank operators, and derives the exact approximation gap and a local Gaussian boundary. CARS estimates reproducible directional signal from training pairs to pick between them.
lDwFVzYN2W.key_idea: Dual projections win exactly when squared directional signal exceeds the estimation cost of their extra degrees of freedom; CARS estimates that signal by cross-fitting on training pairs.
lDwFVzYN2W.evidence: Retrieval experiments across multiple datasets and embedding models, controlled query rotations, rank and sample-size grids, and 168 operator-risk curves.
lDwFVzYN2W.claimed_gains: The Dual-minus-Shared NDCG@10 advantage more than doubles as query rotation grows from 0 to 90 degrees, Dual wins all 32 cells at n=1024 and 2048 versus Shared winning 13 of 16 at n=32, and CARS reduces held-out regret by 49-96% versus fixed-geometry baselines.
lDwFVzYN2W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the operator-based theory gives a precise account of the sharing trade-off and that experiments test specific predictions across models and datasets.
lDwFVzYN2W.main_concern: A theory-practice gap remains: CARS is evaluated on a Frobenius operator-loss surrogate rather than NDCG@10 or against validation-based selection, and the local Gaussian assumptions are detached from real retrieval training.

UZ0c2ROn9a.one_liner: Folds pairwise and global relations into node-only latent fields and generates graphs by self-conditioned flow matching on them.
UZ0c2ROn9a.problem: Graph diffusion and flow models keep O(n^2) pair-level states throughout generation, and existing latent graph generators lack relational representations rich enough to preserve structure under node-only transport.
UZ0c2ROn9a.method: GRAFT constructs relational node fields that fold pairwise and global relational information into node representations, then transports them with Flow Matching using self-conditioning, so the whole generative trajectory stays node-only.
UZ0c2ROn9a.key_idea: Encode edge and global information inside node representations so generation runs on node-only latents with self-conditioned flow matching, lowering cost from quadratic to linear in nodes.
UZ0c2ROn9a.evidence: Generic, molecular, and protein graph benchmarks (from reviews), with sampling time and peak GPU memory measured on Protein.
UZ0c2ROn9a.claimed_gains: On Protein, GRAFT samples a graph in 0.290 s with 110.6 MiB peak GPU memory, 2.1x to 148.7x faster and 1.9x to 5.7x lower in peak memory than the evaluated methods.
UZ0c2ROn9a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree GRAFT removes the quadratic bottleneck of graph diffusion while staying competitive in quality, with strong results across graph domains.
UZ0c2ROn9a.main_concern: The scalability benefit is shown only on small graphs where full-graph models already nearly saturate, a stronger baseline (GraphBSI) wins on some metrics, and the novelty is seen as narrow.

6Uw4rxNI0Z.one_liner: Benchmark of naturally occurring spontaneous speech for Amharic, Oromo, Somali, and Tigrinya ASR evaluation.
6Uw4rxNI0Z.problem: African-language ASR benchmarks use read, single-speaker, or elicited speech, and FLEURS has one gender per split, 3 to 7 speakers per language, and every development speaker also in the test split.
6Uw4rxNI0Z.method: Horn-ASR has 1,000 curated segments per language (15.43 h in total) from 1,710 public interviews, balanced for gender and diverse across dialect and topic. Six multilingual ASR systems from three providers are evaluated under one protocol.
6Uw4rxNI0Z.key_idea: Build the test set from naturally occurring broadcasts and interviews, balanced for gender, dialect, and domain, so evaluation reflects real spontaneous speech rather than read speech.
6Uw4rxNI0Z.evidence: Six multilingual ASR systems from three providers, a comparison with FLEURS on shared model-language pairs, and analyses of gender, dialect, transcription quality, and normalization.
6Uw4rxNI0Z.claimed_gains: The best WER on any language is 0.275, and where a system is scored on both benchmarks its WER is on average 0.16 higher on Horn-ASR than on FLEURS.
6Uw4rxNI0Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a real gap with spontaneous speech, subgroup labels, a concrete FLEURS comparison, and transparent annotation analysis.
6Uw4rxNI0Z.main_concern: Reference reliability and release are questionable: independent human transcripts disagree by 25-48% WER so reference accuracy is not established, plus reporting mismatches, unclear consent and rights, and an inaccessible repository.

MfCjnGNkqh.one_liner: SLiSDE stacks structured linear SDE layers with gated in-flow coupling for parallel-in-time simulation, plus an optional Girsanov tilt.
MfCjnGNkqh.problem: Generic neural drift and diffusion networks are costly to simulate on long horizons and give unstable gradients when the training signal is a path functional rather than a pointwise observation.
MfCjnGNkqh.method: Neural SDEs are built from structured linear stochastic layers simulated in parallel in time at the layer level, with expressivity recovered by gated in-flow stacking where previous-layer paths modulate the next layer's latent flow. For functional calibration where rare paths dominate the loss, an optional Girsanov tilt acts as a learned importance sampler with exact likelihood-ratio correction.
MfCjnGNkqh.key_idea: Make each layer linear-in-state so simulation is an associative scan, and add nonlinearity only through gates from previous-layer paths.
MfCjnGNkqh.evidence: Proofs of well-posedness, a discretisation error bound, validity of the change of measure and a universality result (terminal laws dense in square-integrable laws), plus experiments on functional calibration benchmarks against fully neural SDE baselines.
MfCjnGNkqh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the construction novel and substantial, with O(log T) parallel depth via associative scan while gated stacking retains expressivity.
MfCjnGNkqh.main_concern: Empirical benefits over neural SDE baselines are not clearly established (runtime gains do not always appear, e.g., the 3-layer DAX experiment) and baseline hyperparameter tuning may not be on an equal footing.

y5DliUgRf2.one_liner: Federated training penalizes drift of clients' latent features from a shared sparse autoencoder refit after each aggregation.
y5DliUgRf2.problem: Under feature skew and superposition, FedAvg parameter averaging reduces feature strength and causes cross-client feature interference.
y5DliUgRf2.method: A two-phase procedure uses a sparse autoencoder shared across clients to penalize changes in clients' latent representations during local training, and refits the SAE to the merged model's activations after each aggregation without changing the deployed architecture.
y5DliUgRf2.key_idea: A shared SAE refit on the merged model's activations gives clients a common reference for latent feature directions, penalizing local drift away from it.
y5DliUgRf2.evidence: A controlled toy model of superposition measuring feature shrinkage and interference, and real-data reconstruction on Office-Caltech10 with four clients, across four FL baselines.
y5DliUgRf2.claimed_gains: In the synthetic setting, reduces endpoint reconstruction error by 14.82% and preserves more feature strength after aggregation; further results are cut off in the abstract.
y5DliUgRf2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the analysis of feature shrinkage and interference an interesting explanation of why parameter averaging hurts, and the method combinable with existing FL methods, with consistent gains across four baselines.
y5DliUgRf2.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to reconstruction tasks with very few clients (two synthetic, four on Office-Caltech10), and it is unclear that SAE reconstruction aligns features rather than acting as general regularization.

t7CI3S8Ms3.one_liner: Policy-gradient estimator that exactly averages exponentially many same-solution vertex orders in polynomial time for graph-transformer independent-set training.
t7CI3S8Ms3.problem: Policy-gradient training gives different signals to different vertex orders that build the same independent set, adding order-dependent noise, and averaging them requires accounting for the graph deletions of every alternative.
t7CI3S8Ms3.method: SOM trains from a broad family of same-solution orders while sharing their graph computation. For policies with fixed vertex selection rates, it represents when each vertex remains available across alternative starting positions, so order probabilities and vertex derivatives come without rebuilding the graph for each start.
t7CI3S8Ms3.key_idea: Share graph-deletion computation across same-solution orders via cyclic records and shared mass tables, marginalizing K2^K orders exactly in O(n+m+K^2) operations.
t7CI3S8Ms3.evidence: Theory (preserved expected-reward gradient, covariance reduction under matched sampling, a unit-rate star separation) and weighted vehicle-routing conflict graphs using a GraphGPS-SOM initializer followed by CHILS.
t7CI3S8Ms3.claimed_gains: Exactly averages K2^K orders for a 2K-vertex solution in O(n+m+K^2) operations; GraphGPS-SOM followed by CHILS has a mean normalized-value difference of -0.02% from native CHILS (abstract truncated).
t7CI3S8Ms3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exact marginalization over an exponential equivalence class at polynomial cost is a neat, well-motivated contribution backed by theoretical analysis.
t7CI3S8Ms3.main_concern: The paper is hard to follow (dense Section 3, unclear figures and experiment takeaways), and gains in final solution quality over native solvers are not established.

YZTklAYYcK.one_liner: PerceptBench compares emotion-prompted, accented, and signal-edited speech as jailbreak surfaces for end-to-end audio-language models using jailbreak coverage.
YZTklAYYcK.problem: End-to-end audio-language models use how words are spoken, so a safety policy must stay consistent across more forms of the same request, an added burden the authors call the perceptual bandwidth tax.
YZTklAYYcK.method: Holding request text fixed, they compare Direct TTS, six signal edits, and six emotion prompts, plus a separate accent study, measuring jailbreak coverage (distinct harmful requests reached) with attack success rate and audio quality alongside.
YZTklAYYcK.key_idea: Measure jailbreak coverage, the number of distinct harmful requests a speech surface reaches, using reproducible speech variations instead of gradients or per-request optimization.
YZTklAYYcK.evidence: Two unsafe benchmarks (JailbreakBench and SORRY-Bench) and seven open models, with emotion prompts selected through acoustic-cue screening and quality assessed with NISQA.
YZTklAYYcK.claimed_gains: Emotion prompting reaches more items than editing on six of seven models in JailbreakBench; on Step-Audio 2 it reaches 60 of 100 SORRY-Bench items (35 missed by both Direct TTS and editing) versus 23 for editing, with mean NISQA MOS 4.10 versus 2.81.
YZTklAYYcK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the within-model safety-consistency question is useful and that the controlled setup (fixed text, TTS model, and speaker; prompts chosen on non-benchmark material) makes the emotion-coverage finding consequential.
YZTklAYYcK.main_concern: Coverage is a union over renders so families with more conditions get more attempts, and the effect rests on one TTS system, one judge model without agreement checks, and an unestablished causal mechanism.

FDitFfgFgK.one_liner: Bounds when in-context constitutional clauses approximate the distribution shift from alignment fine-tuning, via fit, interpreter, and interaction errors.
FDitFfgFgK.problem: Alignment training changes weights, yet much test-time steering happens in context, and it is unclear when supplied clauses can approximate parameter-update-induced distribution shifts.
FDitFfgFgK.method: The theory upper bounds approximation error through three components: the retrieved clauses match the update, the frozen model realizes their declared effects, and the clauses retain those effects when combined. Experiments test clause retrieval, context interventions, and a teacher context for constitutional on-policy self-distillation.
FDitFfgFgK.key_idea: Decompose the gap between an in-context clause and a weight update into clause-retrieval fit, model interpretation of declared effects, and clause interaction errors.
FDitFfgFgK.evidence: Four sets of experiments on frozen Qwen3 models, including measurements of all three components across 12 models, context interventions, and constitutional on-policy self-distillation.
FDitFfgFgK.claimed_gains: Retrieving the relevant clause cuts per-token total variation distance to the aligned models from about 0.87 to below 0.02, and context interventions improve balanced safety scores by up to 8.06 percentage points (p<0.001).
FDitFfgFgK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is rigorous and clearly presented, with explicit assumptions, detailed proofs partly formalized in Lean, and an intuitive error decomposition.
FDitFfgFgK.main_concern: Empirical evidence is narrow, relying on synthetic tasks with oracle or literal-name clause retrieval and not quantitatively instantiating the bound, while the theory assumes linear attention heads.

OTp0pTawnX.one_liner: Controlled study separating knowledge access from knowledge presentation to test what shapes LLM-generated scientific ideas.
OTp0pTawnX.problem: Comparing complete AI-scientist systems changes the delivered evidence and its arrangement at once, so it is unclear which organizational choice shapes the resulting ideas.
OTp0pTawnX.method: The framework varies knowledge access (what evidence reaches the model under a fixed budget) independently of knowledge presentation (how the same evidence is arranged), run on ResearchBench and in multi-step development built on CHIMERA with three generators and two judges.
OTp0pTawnX.key_idea: Hold evidence fixed while varying presentation, and vary access under a fixed budget, to attribute ideation differences to evidence content versus arrangement.
OTp0pTawnX.evidence: More than 68,000 idea generations and 87,000 model evaluations across two studies with three generators and two judges.
OTp0pTawnX.claimed_gains: A recombination instruction raises the rate of explicit citation of knowledge from other research branches by 52-62 percentage points over refinement.
OTp0pTawnX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing knowledge organization into access and presentation avoids multi-factor confounding, with careful statistics including equivalence testing across multiple generator and judge models.
OTp0pTawnX.main_concern: The metrics (reference-hypothesis matching and cross-branch citation) do not measure novelty or scientific value, and the tested knowledge structures are simpler than prior systems such as Chain-of-Ideas or GraphRAG.

GjbqKYphGW.one_liner: Sends only the lowest-frequency cosine components of each VLA action chunk and rebuilds the full chunk on the robot.
GjbqKYphGW.problem: When a VLA policy runs on a remote server, every action chunk is sent in full, and how much of a chunk the robot needs to complete its task has rarely been examined.
GjbqKYphGW.method: Frequency-prefix execution is training-free: it transmits only the low-frequency part of each chunk, and the robot rebuilds and executes the whole chunk under the unchanged policy and call schedule. The paper also proposes PairGap to certify prefix regret at single states.
GjbqKYphGW.key_idea: Truncate each action chunk's discrete cosine transform to its lowest-frequency rows, since rebuilt-chunk error equals the energy of the omitted frequencies.
GjbqKYphGW.evidence: Theory bounding rebuilt-chunk error and episode drift, and closed-loop LIBERO experiments (Spatial, Object, Goal, long-horizon) with OpenVLA-OFT and pi-0.5 policies, compared with fewer-step execution.
GjbqKYphGW.claimed_gains: Stays non-inferior to full codes on LIBERO Spatial and LIBERO-10 at 54% and 72% of the payload, and with OpenVLA-OFT the two-frequency message costs 29% fewer bits than the full chunk under FAST+.
GjbqKYphGW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the closed-loop experiment clean, paired, and properly reported, with the finding that two frequency rows suffice on short-horizon suites and four are needed on LIBERO-10.
GjbqKYphGW.main_concern: The motivation is not established: savings are a few hundred bits per message, no latency or bandwidth-limited setting is measured, and the 54% headline is against the authors' own codec rather than FAST+.

wrJnzLuGPe.one_liner: LEAP-HGN detects money laundering with a spatio-temporal hypergraph, brain-inspired amygdala-parietal pathways and LLM-evolved expert rules.
wrJnzLuGPe.problem: Money laundering has become time-sensitive, dense micro-circulation that challenges GNNs through discrete time slices breaking continuity, business noise drowning signals, and strategies evolving faster than rules.
wrJnzLuGPe.method: It builds a spatio-temporal multi-view hypergraph; an amygdala low pathway turns expert rules into warning factors via neural gain modulation before feature propagation, while a parietal high pathway uses Markov high-order diffusion and residual attention. An LLM component refines rules from summaries of missed positive cases.
wrJnzLuGPe.key_idea: Amplify sparse high-risk nodes with rule-derived gain modulation before propagation, then reason with high-order diffusion and attention, while an LLM refines rules from missed cases.
wrJnzLuGPe.evidence: Chronological out-of-time evaluation with laundering templates restricted to training positives, compared with baselines such as ARC, EdgePrompt and Fraud-R1 per reviews, plus component-removal ablations; datasets are not stated in the excerpt.
wrJnzLuGPe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically important, that combining interpretable rule priors with graph learning refined from missed cases is worthwhile, and that the out-of-time evaluation guards against temporal leakage.
wrJnzLuGPe.main_concern: Technical novelty is limited to integrating established components, and the comparison with adapted LLM-based baselines is insufficiently explained.

3UaIlAC4BH.one_liner: Models spatial multi-omics latent geometry as context-regulated synchronization on a hypersphere using location-specific contextual references.
3UaIlAC4BH.problem: Existing geometry organization for spatial multi-omics domain identification relies on inter-location relations or shared semantic references and gives location-specific multimodal and multiscale context no direct role.
3UaIlAC4BH.method: CSR builds location-specific contextual references from multimodal representations and multiscale graph contexts and combines them with relational graph coupling to regulate representation evolution on the hypersphere. The continuous dynamics monotonically decrease the associated objective, and the contextual references impose location-dependent stationary conditions.
3UaIlAC4BH.key_idea: Representations evolve by Riemannian gradient-flow synchronization on a hypersphere, with graph coupling plus per-location contextual anchors setting location-dependent stationary points.
3UaIlAC4BH.evidence: Spatial multi-omics benchmarks with baselines, ablations, sensitivity analysis, qualitative comparisons and efficiency analysis per reviews, plus a monotonic energy-descent theorem.
3UaIlAC4BH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and the empirical evaluation is fairly comprehensive, with strong clustering performance from a context-aware design.
3UaIlAC4BH.main_concern: Theory inconsistency and limited novelty: the energy-descent proof has a factor-of-two gradient mismatch with the stated dynamics, and the proofs and the graph-smoothness-plus-anchoring design are seen as routine.

iqoI6HuvhC.one_liner: Event-camera optical flow splits a dynamic scene into static, rigid, and free regions, giving Gaussians flow-supervised rigid motion.
iqoI6HuvhC.problem: A single deformation field applied to every point in deformation-based dynamic Gaussian Splatting makes fast-moving objects lose pattern detail or blur instead of showing a clear trajectory.
iqoI6HuvhC.method: The method estimates dynamic vision optical flow from events by contrast maximization, derives an observability matrix from contrast curvature to expose the aperture problem, groups patches whose motion a single affine model explains along observable directions, and links groups into tracks. Gaussians are assigned to static, rigid, or free regions by rendering-weight voting; static ones optimize time-invariant geometry, rigid ones follow flow-supervised rigid trajectories, and free ones keep a deformation field.
iqoI6HuvhC.key_idea: Group event-flow patches by whether one affine motion explains them along their observable directions, then give each group's Gaussians a shared rigid trajectory supervised by flow.
iqoI6HuvhC.evidence: Real RGB-event sequences, with ablations on motion groups, completion, and seeding, comparisons of dynamic-region PSNR and LPIPS against baselines, and GMFlow-based flow diagnostics in the appendix.
iqoI6HuvhC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the physical motivation (directional observability for the aperture problem, shared rigid trajectories) is clear and the pipeline is coherent, with improved dynamic-region rendering over deformation baselines.
iqoI6HuvhC.main_concern: Comparison with DEGS, which also uses event-derived flow for dynamic Gaussians, and with anchor-based motion-sharing methods is missing, and the contribution of directional observability to final reconstruction is not isolated.

Epr9UFbCbv.one_liner: Stratified query-relative boundary coordinates and a zero-initialized projection augment global neural operators for 3D indoor airflow prediction.
Epr9UFbCbv.problem: Global neural operators model room-scale airflow without explicitly giving each query point the geometry of nearby flow-driving boundaries such as small supply and return diffusers.
Epr9UFbCbv.method: The Local-Global Operator (LGO) encodes query-relative boundary coordinates stratified by boundary type to preserve small supply and return patches, injecting them into a host neural operator through a zero-initialized projection. This design keeps initial predictions identical to the host operator while adding about 1% more parameters.
Epr9UFbCbv.key_idea: Encode query-relative boundary coordinates stratified by boundary type and inject them into a host neural operator through a zero-initialized projection.
Epr9UFbCbv.evidence: Evaluated across three neural-operator architectures on CFD simulations of a single room with varying diffuser layouts under separation-controlled train-test splits, plus an additional ShapeNet-Car experiment.
Epr9UFbCbv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that conditioning neural operators on local boundary geometry is well motivated and improves full-field velocity predictions across three backbones, particularly on geometrically separated layouts.
Epr9UFbCbv.main_concern: Reviewers question methodological distinction from prior local-global and boundary-conditioned neural operators such as GINO, GNOT, RIGNO, PINTO, and MeshGraphNets.

Repruhd3lg.one_liner: Reparameterizing and factorizing trader-population parameters calibrates executable limit-order-book agent populations against empirical market stylized facts.
Repruhd3lg.problem: Data-driven market models obscure participant-level mechanisms, whereas agent-based financial simulators typically start from prescribed trader populations rather than populations grounded in empirical market evidence.
Repruhd3lg.method: MarketPop separates search coordinates from market representation by reparameterizing constrained resource allocations, factorizing high-dimensional variation into shared directions, and decoding every proposal into a valid heterogeneous trader population. Candidate populations are simulated in an executable limit-order-book market and calibrated against observed stylized facts.
Repruhd3lg.key_idea: Reparameterize constrained allocations and factorize shared variation directions so search proposals decode into complete, valid trader populations calibrated by limit-order-book simulation against market stylized facts.
Repruhd3lg.evidence: Evaluated in a limit-order-book simulator against Direct-X and Joint-Z search baselines on matching five stylized facts over a five-day calibration horizon and three continuation days.
Repruhd3lg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value linking empirical calibration to an executable heterogeneous trader population through a structured search parameterization and valid population decoder.
