Repruhd3lg.main_concern: Reviewers point out that calibrating only initial endowments matches or slightly beats calibrating all four population layers on held-out discrepancy (4.85 versus 4.89), leaving the benefit of the full hierarchy unclear.

QqnWk3eIcF.one_liner: Injecting hierarchical experience templates at varying guidance levels within GRPO rollout groups trains mobile GUI agents under sparse rewards.
QqnWk3eIcF.problem: Long horizons and sparse rewards in online RL for mobile GUI agents cause GRPO rollout groups to collapse into uniform failure, yielding near-zero advantage and weak learning signals.
QqnWk3eIcF.method: UI-Mem stores workflows, subtask skills, and failure patterns as parameterized templates in an online-updated hierarchical memory and injects retrieved experience at full, partial, or zero strength within each GRPO rollout group. Contrasting these mixed-guidance rollouts creates within-group reward variance that trains the unguided policy to internalize external experience.
QqnWk3eIcF.key_idea: Sample each GRPO rollout group with full, partial, and zero retrieved-experience guidance from an online-updated hierarchical template memory so within-group reward contrasts train the unguided policy.
QqnWk3eIcF.evidence: Evaluated across model scales on AndroidWorld and unseen AndroidLab applications against vanilla GRPO, dense-reward training, and static experience reuse.
QqnWk3eIcF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework addresses GRPO gradient starvation in sparse-reward GUI navigation and produces substantial policy-only improvements on AndroidWorld and unseen AndroidLab apps.
QqnWk3eIcF.main_concern: Reviewers note that the main ablation without stratification gives every rollout full guidance, confounding within-group guidance contrast with the removal of unguided training rollouts.

H7AVY9gPTe.one_liner: Selecting calibrated single-requirement task-derived probes and fitting a score predictor estimates full long-horizon agent benchmark performance cheaply.
H7AVY9gPTe.problem: Long-horizon agent benchmarks require expensive multi-turn model calls, tool invocations, and environment interactions that task-subset selection still runs to completion.
H7AVY9gPTe.method: ProbeCompress builds short, independently verifiable single-requirement probes from the public context of benchmark tasks, selects a small probe suite using calibration-model responses, and fits a full-benchmark score predictor. Evaluating a new agent then requires running only the selected probes rather than complete benchmark trajectories.
H7AVY9gPTe.key_idea: Replace full multi-step benchmark tasks with a calibrated suite of single-requirement, independently verified task-derived probes paired with a fitted benchmark-score predictor.
H7AVY9gPTe.evidence: Evaluated across six agent benchmarks with up to 18 models, including temporal transfer from 14 earlier models to 4 later models and random and generic probe controls.
H7AVY9gPTe.claimed_gains: ProbeCompress predicts full-benchmark scores with 0.028 MAE using 222.1× fewer tokens and 45.7× less execution work than full evaluation (versus 0.030 MAE at ~55× more tokens for the strongest complete-task baseline), and reaches 0.044 MAE without refitting on 4 later models.
H7AVY9gPTe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that replacing complete long-horizon tasks with short task-derived probes is a practical, distinct compression approach backed by thorough controls and transparent setup-cost accounting across six benchmarks.
H7AVY9gPTe.main_concern: Reviewers note that removing environment interaction reduces probes to static reasoning proxies that struggle to rank closely matched models, degrade under model shift, and miss interaction-specific agent differences.

ywgpWIW3v4.one_liner: Posterior validity thresholding of joint tetrad p-values frames high-dimensional proxy discovery in proximal causal learning as acceptance-side multiple testing.
ywgpWIW3v4.problem: High-dimensional proxy discovery in proximal causal learning tests thousands to millions of candidates where the critical error is false validation—retaining invalid proxies that bias causal effect estimates.
ywgpWIW3v4.method: The method computes one joint tetrad p-value per candidate proxy triplet with validity as the null hypothesis, converts p-values into posterior validity probabilities via a two-group mixture model, and accepts candidates above a threshold to target the false validation rate (FVR). It analyzes anti-conservativeness of plug-in null-proportion estimates under weak violations and proves an exact identity equating mean absolute causal bias to FVR times accepted invalid-triplet bias.
ywgpWIW3v4.key_idea: Threshold two-group posterior validity probabilities computed from joint tetrad test p-values to control the false validation rate of accepted confounder proxy triplets.
ywgpWIW3v4.evidence: Supported by oracle FVR guarantees, plug-in anti-conservativeness bounds under weak violations, an exact causal-bias factorization identity, and simulation studies.
ywgpWIW3v4.reviewer_consensus: Domain-familiar reviewers agree that reframing proxy discovery around acceptance-side false validation rate control and linking FVR to causal bias via an exact factorization fits proximal causal learning well.
ywgpWIW3v4.main_concern: Reviewers note that the theoretical results follow closely from standard empirical-Bayes multiple-testing facts while the data-placed cutoff relies on a null-proportion estimator biased in the unsafe anti-conservative direction, alongside dense technical exposition.

ekRph75ol8.one_liner: Distilling validation-gated trajectory lessons teaches ReAct data-analysis agents when to generate and inspect charts alongside textual reasoning.
ekRph75ol8.problem: ReAct-style data-analysis agents conduct intermediate reasoning almost entirely in text and rarely invoke self-generated charts despite being able to read visual trends and anomalies from plots.
ekRph75ol8.method: After diagnosing this capability-use gap on a 200-task controlled suite across four matched interface conditions, the authors distill two experience families from conditioned rollouts covering analytical operation selection and when to invoke text, charts, or both. A trajectory judge labels outcomes and steps, and a validation gate admits only experience lessons that improve held-out accuracy.
ekRph75ol8.key_idea: Distill and validation-gate trajectory experiences from conditioned rollouts to guide data agents on analytical operation selection and when to invoke intermediate chart versus text representations.
ekRph75ol8.evidence: Diagnosed on a 200-task controlled probe suite under four interface conditions and evaluated on three held-out data-analysis benchmarks across four LLM backbones.
ekRph75ol8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating self-generated charts as intermediate epistemic actions is well motivated and that the controlled probe study clearly reveals a capability-versus-use gap.
ekRph75ol8.main_concern: Reviewers point out that intermediate analysis-phase chart generation remains low without causal proof that in-loop charts drive the accuracy gains, compounded by circular reliance on one unvalidated LLM judge for labeling, gating, and evaluation.

ETyLj6o7pz.one_liner: RGFA gates language-model policy updates using the reliability of accumulated feedback evidence.
ETyLj6o7pz.problem: Language models struggle to distinguish informative negative feedback from environmental noise during adaptive decision-making.
ETyLj6o7pz.method: The study compares humans and language models in controlled probabilistic reversal learning. RGFA regulates policy updates according to accumulated feedback reliability to decide when a strategy should change.
ETyLj6o7pz.key_idea: Accumulate feedback evidence and condition policy updates on its estimated reliability.
ETyLj6o7pz.evidence: Controlled human-model comparisons and reversal-learning experiments test stable and volatile conditions with two and four stimuli.
ETyLj6o7pz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled diagnosis of negative-feedback learning and the observed improvements in adapting to environmental changes.
ETyLj6o7pz.main_concern: Evaluation centered on one primary model and one task paradigm provides limited evidence of generalization.

GN0ZGqIKEY.one_liner: ConservGP fits sparse Gaussian-process surrogates and certifies directional uncertainty contracts using outward-rounded continuous-domain calculations.
GN0ZGqIKEY.problem: Gaussian-process compression can alter uncertainty in a direction unsuitable for planning or monitoring despite small average approximation error.
GN0ZGqIKEY.method: ConservGP fits a fixed-size sparse surrogate under a directional variance contract with a chosen margin. Its certifier uses verified linear solves and variance expressions that preserve cancellation, rounding arithmetic outward on both models.
GN0ZGqIKEY.key_idea: Certify a signed teacher-surrogate uncertainty inequality over continuous domains using verified arithmetic that preserves correlated variance cancellation.
GN0ZGqIKEY.evidence: Experiments cover synthetic data, two drone platforms, one-dimensional channels, five problems with two to four inputs, and joint covariance ordering for six-output drone teachers.
GN0ZGqIKEY.claimed_gains: On drone state channels, the surrogate stores 54 times fewer parameters than the teacher.
GN0ZGqIKEY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical relevance of controlling which side of teacher uncertainty a compressed Gaussian process occupies.
GN0ZGqIKEY.main_concern: Practical scalability remains unclear given expensive offline certification and limited evidence for higher-dimensional deployment.

anKFJMIeiL.one_liner: Kite reuses a side-input expert at sparse model depths to update marker states while preserving marker-free host computation.
anKFJMIeiL.problem: Multimodal specialization must incorporate external evidence without consuming the host input sequence or changing behavior when inactive.
anKFJMIeiL.method: A shared side expert reads external evidence and host marker states, updating designated markers at sparse depths under a prompt-level router. The Earth-observation implementation combines frozen DINOv3 features and a frozen host, with marker-free requests bypassing the expert.
anKFJMIeiL.key_idea: Route external evidence through a shared expert that writes only marker states and bypasses all specialization on marker-free requests.
anKFJMIeiL.evidence: Earth-observation evaluations include pre-locked new-site recognition, mismatched-image controls, VRSBench-VQA, RSVQA-LR, placement ablations, and depth probes.
anKFJMIeiL.claimed_gains: Kite exceeds matched host LoRA by +9.8 percentage points, raises the VRSBench-VQA mean from 0.627 to 0.772, and reaches 0.913 on RSVQA-LR.
anKFJMIeiL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the modular specialization design and verifiable preservation of host behavior when the expert is inactive.
anKFJMIeiL.main_concern: The controls do not isolate the shared multi-depth architecture's contribution from visual features, added capacity, and the training recipe.

nJayOwfMMA.one_liner: PolyWorld uses controlled interventions and molecular dynamics to benchmark multimodal reasoning and action choices over evolving polymers.
nJayOwfMMA.problem: Existing scientific multimodal benchmarks rarely test physical changes after interventions or decisions based on those changes.
nJayOwfMMA.method: PolyWorld constructs diverse three-dimensional polymer structures and simulates controlled intervention branches. The resulting questions assess perception, reasoning, decision, and planning, with answers traceable to construction records and simulated outcomes.
nJayOwfMMA.key_idea: Generate alternative polymer trajectories from shared initial states and derive questions about intervention consequences and subsequent actions.
nJayOwfMMA.evidence: The benchmark evaluates multimodal models and human experts on 4,093 questions derived from 5,530 polymer structures and 2,333 unique repeat units.
nJayOwfMMA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value extending polymer evaluation beyond static properties to intervention outcomes and action selection.
nJayOwfMMA.main_concern: The decision and planning tasks do not sufficiently establish that their specifications and visible observations support the selected gold actions.

QpWHmzkGkI.one_liner: Cross-domain inverse-action risks diagnose planning failures hidden by accurate latent world-model predictions.
QpWHmzkGkI.problem: Accurate latent predictions can encode action relationships that fail to transfer to real environment transitions and therefore plan poorly.
QpWHmzkGkI.method: The paper defines action-identifiability through Bayes inverse risk and constructs a 2×2 Action-Consistency Transfer Matrix across real and predicted transition domains. These diagnostics examine action recovery, cross-domain consistency, and model screening.
QpWHmzkGkI.key_idea: Train and evaluate inverse-action probes across real and predicted transition domains to separate action-identifiability from cross-domain consistency.
QpWHmzkGkI.evidence: TwoRoom, PushT, and OGBench-Cube experiments compare diagnostics with prediction loss, intervene on transition domains, and evaluate model-ranking accuracy.
QpWHmzkGkI.claimed_gains: Model screening reaches 98.81% pairwise ranking accuracy for candidates separated by more than 5% success.
QpWHmzkGkI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider action-identifiability and transfer diagnostics useful for understanding and assessing world-model planning.
QpWHmzkGkI.main_concern: The contribution needs clearer differentiation from prior action-consistency and inverse-dynamics supervision methods.

t0Q165QR0K.one_liner: Protected spatial and salient attention structures precede adaptive residual routing for faster autoregressive video diffusion.
t0Q165QR0K.problem: Mean-pooled sparse-attention routing misses concentrated interactions, while changing context selections across chunks can introduce visual discontinuities.
t0Q165QR0K.method: Residual Forcing protects spatially aligned blocks, axial halo tokens, and shared salient keys before routing residual attention with reusable head priors and adaptive budgets. Shared candidate-frame choices and fused sparse kernels support continuity and efficient execution.
t0Q165QR0K.key_idea: Reserve aligned, halo, and salient keys before routing residual blocks with head-level priors and adaptive budgets, sharing frame choices across chunks.
t0Q165QR0K.evidence: LongLive/Wan2.1-1.3B experiments at 480p include component ablations and routing, attention, and end-to-end latency analyses.
t0Q165QR0K.claimed_gains: On LongLive, Residual Forcing achieves a 4.12× self-attention speedup in fixed-cache profiling.
t0Q165QR0K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical inference focus and transparent latency and efficiency analyses.
t0Q165QR0K.main_concern: Reviewers see the method mainly as an incremental combination of existing static and dynamic sparse-attention ideas.

tyD2yhBxlH.one_liner: Dual-view diffusion reconstructs elite coil paths while hard depth-first search enforces geometric feasibility.
tyD2yhBxlH.problem: Electromagnetic inverse-design workflows lack automated initialization of promising feasible coil routes under limited simulation budgets.
tyD2yhBxlH.method: Sequence and spatial diffusion views model route order and occupancy, with quality-weighted residual learning constrained around a frozen geometry base. Hard depth-first search filters actions and backtracks, while validated paths update an elite archive for later reconstruction rounds.
tyD2yhBxlH.key_idea: Inpaint elite routes using performance-guided diffusion, enforce hard geometric constraints during search, and recycle evaluated candidates as reconstruction parents.
tyD2yhBxlH.evidence: The benchmark spans symmetric enclosing, asymmetric enclosing, and non-enclosing scenes, three label budgets, and five repetitions, with learning-component ablations.
tyD2yhBxlH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard automated initialization for electromagnetic coil design as a meaningful practical problem.
tyD2yhBxlH.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate the diffusion and preference-learning benefits from the elite-search machinery or simpler non-diffusion alternatives.

iqtsRZhiqq.one_liner: Linearly increasing adapter rank with depth allocates face-recognition adaptation capacity according to measured layerwise rank demand.
iqtsRZhiqq.problem: Uniform-rank adapters underuse shallow-block capacity while saturating deeper blocks during foundation-model adaptation for face recognition.
iqtsRZhiqq.method: Spectral probing motivates a search-free linear increase in adapter rank with network depth. Rank-stabilized scaling yields DG-LoRA and DG-DoRA implementations for vision foundation models.
iqtsRZhiqq.key_idea: Increase adapter rank linearly with transformer depth instead of assigning the same rank to every block.
iqtsRZhiqq.evidence: Experiments study eight ViT-L foundation models, adapter-rank diagnostics, budget comparisons, and face-recognition training on WebFace4M.
iqtsRZhiqq.claimed_gains: With 14M trainable parameters, the WebFace4M-trained model reaches 95.3% TAR on IJB-C at FAR=10^{-4}.
iqtsRZhiqq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the rank-probing evidence and motivation for allocating more capacity to deeper blocks convincing.
iqtsRZhiqq.main_concern: Matched-budget comparisons and inconsistent training settings do not convincingly isolate a benefit from depth-graded allocation itself.

QBSQcYotIw.one_liner: ETAPS alternates progressive pruning with fixed-budget sparse adaptation, using adapted gradients to guide subsequent weight removal.
QBSQcYotIw.problem: Extreme sparsity creates a trade-off between one-shot pruning's quality loss and end-to-end mask optimization's model-sized state.
QBSQcYotIw.method: ETAPS progressively tightens a global sparsity constraint while training a sparse delta under a small fixed budget. Adaptation compensates for incremental removals and supplies end-to-end gradients for the next pruning stage.
QBSQcYotIw.key_idea: Keep each pruning step small enough for sparse-delta adaptation to compensate, then use the adapted model's gradients for subsequent pruning.
QBSQcYotIw.evidence: Experiments compare six models from 125M to 13B across 50% to 90% sparsity and include controlled recipe ablations.
QBSQcYotIw.claimed_gains: ETAPS reports perplexity reductions of up to 42% over ELSA and prunes LLaMA-2-7B at 90% sparsity on a single H200 where ELSA uses four.
QBSQcYotIw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent perplexity improvements and a useful quality-cost trade-off at high sparsity.
QBSQcYotIw.main_concern: The method combines established pruning and adaptation components, with insufficient matched comparisons to isolate the sparse-adaptation choice.

Tygnjcgtd2.one_liner: Accumulated watermarks in model-generated outputs trigger delayed backdoor behavior when the model re-ingests its own work.
Tygnjcgtd2.problem: Conventional backdoors require attacker access after deployment or accurate anticipation of externally supplied triggers.
Tygnjcgtd2.method: The method trains models to generate and recognize watermarked outputs, using accumulated watermark strength as an activation signal. Repeated generation and re-ingestion in agent workflows can build the signal without a new attacker-supplied trigger.
Tygnjcgtd2.key_idea: Make a model's own persistent watermarked outputs accumulate into the signal that activates its backdoor.
Tygnjcgtd2.evidence: Evaluation covers 3 model families and 3 scenarios, including controlled experiments and end-to-end coding tasks in an agent harness.
Tygnjcgtd2.claimed_gains: The method reports near-100% attack success rate across 3 model families and 3 scenarios while preserving benign behavior before activation.
Tygnjcgtd2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find self-generated accumulating triggers a meaningful extension of the backdoor threat model for agents.
Tygnjcgtd2.main_concern: The end-to-end demonstration relies on a harness intervention that prompts read-back, leaving natural activation without intervention unestablished.

G2HBCKp9Bd.one_liner: Increasing Adam epsilon only for output embeddings suppresses updates to rarely used vocabulary during domain adaptation.
G2HBCKp9Bd.problem: Vocabulary-deficient adaptation data can drive catastrophic forgetting even when original training data are unavailable for replay.
G2HBCKp9Bd.method: Parameter-freezing experiments localize much forgetting to output embeddings of tokens rarely used in new data. The intervention raises Adam's epsilon to 1 × 10−4 only on output embeddings to suppress amplified small-gradient updates.
G2HBCKp9Bd.key_idea: Increase the optimizer denominator offset for output embeddings to prevent small, persistent softmax gradients from producing large updates.
G2HBCKp9Bd.evidence: Localization experiments span six models up to 1.4B parameters, and intervention tests cover eight settings from 160M to 12B across four model families.
G2HBCKp9Bd.claimed_gains: The epsilon change removes 39.0% to 67.8% of forgetting across eight settings, preserves target learning in seven of the eight, and improves old-task accuracy in all eight.
G2HBCKp9Bd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled localization of forgetting to output embeddings and the simple optimizer-level intervention.
G2HBCKp9Bd.main_concern: Broad forgetting claims exceed evidence concentrated in a specific language-shift setting and primarily loss-based measurements.

QYsWSftf2w.one_liner: Image-response sampling, linear cross-attention, and uncertainty-aware distillation reduce LiDAR-camera detection costs.
QYsWSftf2w.problem: Redundant inputs and costly cross-modal interactions impede real-time detection, while indiscriminate input reduction discards useful observations.
QYsWSftf2w.method: LMF-3DDet selects LiDAR points using image detection heatmaps with geometric dilation and fuses them with image features through kernelized linear cross-attention. A full-input teacher supplies uncertainty-weighted training supervision without participating at inference.
QYsWSftf2w.key_idea: Select points near image-response seeds, fuse them without dense pairwise attention, and distill full-input teacher knowledge into the reduced-input student.
QYsWSftf2w.evidence: nuScenes and Waymo evaluations include accuracy-efficiency measurements and ablations of sampling, fusion, and distillation.
QYsWSftf2w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the modular treatment of input processing, cross-modal interaction, and training-only knowledge transfer.
QYsWSftf2w.main_concern: Single-camera coverage and differing baseline input configurations make benchmark comparability and treatment of out-of-view objects unclear.

VBuqRJIIHa.one_liner: ProxFill replaces nearby invalid XYZ entries with valid neighbors to repair depth-encoding confounds in RGB-D segmentation.
VBuqRJIIHa.problem: Encoding missing depth as the camera-origin point creates artificial geometry and distorts robustness comparisons.
VBuqRJIIHa.method: The study isolates invalid-depth encoding through controlled ablations and constructs corruptions matched to observed missing-depth patterns. ProxFill copies the nearest valid pixel's XYZ triplet only within an image-distance threshold fixed on a disjoint development split.
VBuqRJIIHa.key_idea: Replace invalid origin-valued depth points with the nearest valid XYZ triplet only when the image-space distance falls below a fixed threshold.
VBuqRJIIHa.evidence: Experiments examine OCID and OSD, controlled encoding interventions, calibrated degradation, official UCN+ checkpoints, and transfer to MSMFormer.
VBuqRJIIHa.claimed_gains: ProxFill improves OSD by 2.8 Object-F and 6.9 Boundary-F points, keeps corrected models within one Object-F point under degradation versus 14–16-point losses, and reduces measured UCN processing latency by 25%.
VBuqRJIIHa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical diagnosis that invalid-depth representation can confound segmentation and robustness evaluation.
VBuqRJIIHa.main_concern: The sensor-calibrated corruption protocol and generalization across sensor acquisition conditions are insufficiently validated.

yOQsePuglD.one_liner: Propagation-aware singular-direction ranking and joint rank allocation compress gradient proxies for LLM training-data selection.
yOQsePuglD.problem: Independent matrix compression ignores errors propagated across layers that can change gradient-alignment rankings used for data selection.
yOQsePuglD.method: LPEC ranks retained low-rank directions using singular values and their propagated removal errors. It allocates ranks jointly across weight matrices under a shared parameter budget to build a compressed gradient proxy.
yOQsePuglD.key_idea: Estimate cross-layer effects of removed singular directions and allocate compression ranks where retained components reduce propagated error most.
yOQsePuglD.evidence: The study includes conditional theoretical analysis and experiments across LLM families and downstream tasks, with a Dolly aggregation control.
yOQsePuglD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value explicitly modeling cross-layer compression effects in both direction selection and rank allocation.
yOQsePuglD.main_concern: Main comparisons change gradient-score aggregation as well as compression, so observed gains cannot be attributed cleanly to LPEC.

jHTw5SssMw.one_liner: DAWN-Cast evolves wavelet scale families through separate temporal blocks before reconciling them with spectral and spatial refinement.
jHTw5SssMw.problem: Existing precipitation nowcasting models capture spatial scales without assigning distinct temporal dynamics to differently persistent rain structures.
jHTw5SssMw.method: Wavelet Guided Temporal Modeling decomposes radar features into scale families, each processed independently by an MLP and adaptive history-selective Gabor mapping. A subsequent refinement stage combines global spectral and local spatial interactions across the evolved scales.
jHTw5SssMw.key_idea: Independent scale-specific temporal operators evolve wavelet features before cross-scale reconstruction and spatial refinement.
jHTw5SssMw.evidence: Experiments compare eleven baselines on four datasets, including SEVIR, with zero-shot transfer, scale-persistence analysis, pure-advection controls, and temporal-block ablations.
jHTw5SssMw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find scale-dependent temporal persistence a clear motivation and acknowledge strong multi-dataset results and useful supporting analyses.
jHTw5SssMw.main_concern: Ablations change wavelet depth alongside temporal weight sharing, so they do not isolate the benefit of independent temporal operators.

Yqlat1Pr1u.one_liner: Iteratively prunes minimally impactful attention heads from an active intervention set to construct interaction-aware function vectors.
Yqlat1Pr1u.problem: Selecting function-vector attention heads independently using marginal importance scores ignores inter-head interactions, leading to redundant or suboptimally combined head subsets.
Yqlat1Pr1u.method: CORE-FV (Conditional Ordering through Removal Evaluation for Function Vectors) evaluates each attention head conditioned on the remaining active intervention set. Using an adaptive backward refinement schedule, it iteratively removes heads whose deletion minimally degrades induced task behavior to produce an interaction-aware head ordering.
Yqlat1Pr1u.key_idea: Perform adaptive backward head deletion that re-evaluates each attention head conditioned on the remaining intervention set rather than ranking heads by marginal indirect effect.
Yqlat1Pr1u.evidence: Evaluated across eight in-context learning transformations, composite sequential/parallel tasks, and multiple open-weight LLM families (including Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B) against a matched Average Indirect Effect (AIE) baseline.
Yqlat1Pr1u.claimed_gains: Achieves average accuracy gains of up to 11.84 percentage points over a matched Average Indirect Effect baseline across eight ICL transformations, and raises composite-task average accuracy on Llama-3.1-8B from 41.81% to 87.34%.
Yqlat1Pr1u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that conditional backward head selection is conceptually clean, plugs directly into the standard Function Vector pipeline, and captures head dependencies effectively on composite tasks.
Yqlat1Pr1u.main_concern: Repeated white-box intervention evaluations add unquantified head-selection compute overhead, improvements are inconsistent across standard model-task pairs, and comparisons to recent joint head-attribution methods are missing.

CIUzfMYMfq.one_liner: Detects malicious LLM agent skills statically by checking consistency between SKILL.md capability declarations and extracted code/instruction flows.
CIUzfMYMfq.problem: Dynamic vetting of LLM agent skills incurs high execution time and token costs, while capability-only static scanners produce false positives because benign skills also perform security-sensitive operations.
CIUzfMYMfq.method: The proposed framework extracts declared capabilities from SKILL.md and identifies security-sensitive source-to-sink behaviors across bundled scripts, files, and natural-language instructions. A declaration-behavior consistency analysis then flags mismatches between declared and actual behaviors along with their corresponding source, sink, and declaration evidence.
CIUzfMYMfq.key_idea: Compare capabilities declared in SKILL.md against security-sensitive source-to-sink behaviors extracted across code, files, and instructions to flag undeclared operations.
CIUzfMYMfq.evidence: Evaluated on 5,520 agent skills (SkillTrustBench with Qwen-plus per reviews) against five static-analysis baselines, including ablations and adversarial evasion tests.
CIUzfMYMfq.claimed_gains: Achieves an F1 score of 0.946 on 5,520 evaluated skills, outperforming five static-analysis baselines.
CIUzfMYMfq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting static skill vetting from raw capability detection to undeclared data/control flows is practical, training-free, and produces auditable evidence.
CIUzfMYMfq.main_concern: Evaluation relies on a single benchmark and LLM backend without full comparisons to published skill scanners, omits token and latency scan-cost reporting, and remains vulnerable to adaptive attackers who co-modify SKILL.md and code.

U7QGsy0J1E.one_liner: Proves weighted conditional flow matching can exclude all endpoint-correct affine generators and introduces an endpoint moment estimator.
U7QGsy0J1E.problem: Regression-based conditional flow matching (CFM) can fail to select any endpoint-correct generator even when the model class contains one and arbitrary input-measurable positive-definite loss weights are allowed.
U7QGsy0J1E.method: The authors construct a finite-dimensional affine velocity class for straight-line Gaussian-endpoint CFM where every admissible positive-definite weight excludes the correct generator, characterize exact spectral-contrast conditions and diverging asymptotic variance for reweighted selection, and propose an endpoint-derived moment equation using the same data that stays regular at the obstruction.
U7QGsy0J1E.key_idea: Construct affine velocity classes where input-measurable positive-definite regression weights exclude every endpoint-correct generator, and replace singular weighted regression with an endpoint-derived moment equation.
U7QGsy0J1E.evidence: Theoretical whole-set exclusion and asymptotic-variance proofs for affine velocity classes, alongside controlled finite-update experiments on structured synthetic families and a pretrained CIFAR-10 teacher setup.
U7QGsy0J1E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing endpoint realizability from regression-objective selection in conditional flow matching is rigorously formulated, with sharp exclusion and reweighting characterizations.
U7QGsy0J1E.main_concern: The theoretical obstruction relies on restricted low-dimensional affine velocity parameterizations, and neural experiments are limited to narrow finite-update teacher-target diagnostics rather than standard real-data flow training.

Ty5waKV0qC.one_liner: Routes forecasting windows across growing time-series foundation model zoos without training via anchor-mapped capability retrieval and rank fusion.
Ty5waKV0qC.problem: Routing across evolving time-series foundation model zoos faces high online inference cost if forwarding all candidates, or repeated relabeling and retraining costs if using supervised selectors.
Ty5waKV0qC.method: TSRouter uses source-stratified probe anchors to map model-specific capability regions in a fixed shared representation space (PROFILE), retrieves local preferences for unseen task windows and aggregates them via window/channel rank fusion (ROUTE), and integrates newly added models by evaluating them only on existing anchors without retraining (INSERT).
Ty5waKV0qC.key_idea: Map model forecasting strengths over source-stratified probe anchors in a fixed representation space and fuse retrieved local anchor preferences across windows and channels without training a selector.
Ty5waKV0qC.evidence: Evaluated across 97 forecasting configurations from 23 datasets and a 20-model time-series foundation model zoo with ablations on Fourier features, anchors, and routing overhead.
Ty5waKV0qC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the training-free PROFILE/ROUTE/INSERT decomposition practical for incrementally adding new time-series foundation models without selector retraining, achieving strong forecasting ranks at low overhead.
Ty5waKV0qC.main_concern: The paper omits comparisons and novelty discussion against closely related time-series routers (such as ZooCast and TimeRouter), lacks statistical significance tests, and does not justify hard capability-region assignments over simpler kNN loss weighting.

ZZafvBGyd3.one_liner: Pairs DC-protected smooth low-frequency gains with local-global complex high-frequency modulation for lightweight cloud workload forecasting.
ZZafvBGyd3.problem: Cloud workload forecasting must adapt slowly varying multi-scale periodic trends while modeling fine-grained high-frequency interactions under tight per-service parameter and compute budgets.
ZZafvBGyd3.method: DuoFreq splits spectral processing asymmetrically into Smooth Low-Frequency Modulation—learning identity-initialized, bounded residual gains with DC protection and smoothness regularization—and Local-Global High-Frequency Modulation, which fuses neighboring-bin spectral features with pooled band-wide context prior to complex-valued spectral transformation.
ZZafvBGyd3.key_idea: Apply bounded, smoothness-constrained residual gains to low frequencies while combining local spectral neighbors and pooled band context before complex-valued transformation on high frequencies.
ZZafvBGyd3.evidence: Evaluated on five real-world cloud workload datasets across four forecasting horizons against eleven baselines, including component ablations, unseen-variable transfer, and CUDA latency benchmarks.
ZZafvBGyd3.claimed_gains: Reduces average MSE by 3.04% and MAE by 1.68% relative to the best-performing baseline per dataset and metric across five cloud workload datasets while using approximately 0.61M parameters at the longest horizon.
ZZafvBGyd3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the asymmetric two-band spectral architecture is lightweight (~0.61M parameters), clearly presented, and broadly evaluated across five cloud workload datasets.
ZZafvBGyd3.main_concern: The paper omits direct baseline comparisons and clear differentiation against closely related frequency-domain cloud forecasters like Fremer and FP-MLP, while low-frequency module ablations show minimal impact and unseen-variable transfer errors appear anomalously lower than in-domain errors.

c9yLcG0MMY.one_liner: Wraps frozen embodied VLA models in a decoupled harness integrating memory-grounded planning, online monitoring, verification, and recovery.
c9yLcG0MMY.problem: Vision-Language-Action models struggle on long-horizon embodied tasks requiring persistent memory and error recovery, while adapting general-purpose agent harnesses leaves embodied execution management underexplored.
c9yLcG0MMY.method: EVA provides a decoupled embodied harness around unmodified policies that integrates perception, structured memory, memory-grounded subtask generation, executor selection, online execution monitoring, outcome verification, and memory-updated replanning or recovery.
c9yLcG0MMY.key_idea: Decouple long-horizon control from frozen embodied policies through step-wise subtask generation, executor selection, online execution monitoring, outcome verification, and memory-updated replanning or recovery.
c9yLcG0MMY.evidence: Theoretical characterization of harness-guided execution alongside experiments across VLA backbones on VLABench, LIBERO-LoHo, RoboMME, and real-world robot tasks.
c9yLcG0MMY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that EVA consistently improves long-horizon task completion across multiple frozen VLA policies and real-world robot evaluations without parameter updates.
c9yLcG0MMY.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited methodological novelty over established closed-loop embodied agent components, cross-backbone confounding in headline comparisons, and potential reliance on privileged simulator resets during recovery.

SWkayh8Vd1.one_liner: Audits G-Retriever graph soft prompts via token-swap controls, revealing input-independent token collapse and proposing two-stage training.
SWkayh8Vd1.problem: In textual graph soft prompting such as G-Retriever, learned GNN graph tokens collapse into nearly indistinguishable, input-independent embeddings when paired with verbalized graph text.
SWkayh8Vd1.method: The authors audit G-Retriever and follow-up multi-token graph-prompting methods using dataset-mean, cross-example, and corrupted-graph token swaps alongside a graph-free learned constant-prompt control. They analyze why collapse emerges at the projection interface and introduce a two-stage training procedure designed to produce non-collapsed graph tokens.
SWkayh8Vd1.key_idea: Use token-replacement interventions and graph-free constant-prompt controls to diagnose projection-step collapse of graph soft tokens into generic input-independent prompts, alongside a two-stage anti-collapse training procedure.
SWkayh8Vd1.evidence: Evaluated across three GraphQA benchmarks (including WebQSP and SceneGraphs per reviews), three graph encoders, two LLM families, and both frozen and LoRA-adapted configurations.
SWkayh8Vd1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnostic protocol—combining token-replacement interventions with a matched graph-free constant prompt—convincingly shows that high GraphQA accuracy can coexist with collapsed, unused graph tokens.
SWkayh8Vd1.main_concern: Preventing token collapse does not consistently improve task accuracy—the proposed two-stage pipeline only matches or underperforms G-Retriever on benchmarks—and swap interventions conflate graph structure with entity semantics.

2Wg61vEs0Q.one_liner: Couples observation-driven sEMG memory and pose-conditioned hand motion prediction asymmetrically without writing predicted poses back to memory.
2Wg61vEs0Q.problem: In streaming surface-EMG hand motion decoding, feeding predicted poses back into recurrent memory propagates prediction errors across future timesteps.
2Wg61vEs0Q.method: MARC combines joint-conditioned sEMG encoding, observation-driven persistent memory updates, and pose-conditioned motion prediction in an asymmetric two-pathway state architecture where predicted poses contribute to decoded output without writing back into observation memory.
2Wg61vEs0Q.key_idea: Update persistent sensor memory strictly from joint-conditioned sEMG observations while conditioning motion prediction on memory without feeding predicted poses back into memory.
2Wg61vEs0Q.evidence: Evaluated on emg2pose, MANUS, and NinaPro DB8 against reproduced TDS+LSTM and EMGFormer-L baselines, paired with controlled pose-error injection and observation-memory-loss interventions.
2Wg61vEs0Q.claimed_gains: On emg2pose, MARC reduces angular error by 9.5–19.3% and fingertip error by 13.1–21.6% relative to TDS+LSTM while improving displacement accuracy and motion direction.
2Wg61vEs0Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear asymmetric separation of observation memory from pose prediction, strong reconstruction accuracy across three sEMG datasets, and controlled error-propagation versus memory-recovery diagnostics.
2Wg61vEs0Q.main_concern: Ablations do not fully isolate asymmetric memory coupling from simultaneous encoder, fusion, and loss changes, artificial pose perturbations may not reflect natural prediction errors, and formal definitions are deferred to the appendix.

aP3ipuT59Y.one_liner: Joint multi-frame slot binding combines shared-prototype all-frame reconstruction with sampled-frame spatial decoding for video object discovery.
aP3ipuT59Y.problem: Adding context frames in per-frame reconstruction setups increases dense spatial decoding cost during video object discovery.
aP3ipuT59Y.method: CoSlot binds features across multiple frames jointly to shared slots instead of learning frame-to-frame transitions. Shared prototypes reconstruct all visible frames from binding assignments while a spatial decoder reconstructs only sampled frames, with slot passing linking inference chunks.
aP3ipuT59Y.key_idea: Bind features across multiple frames jointly to shared slots while reconstructing all visible frames via shared prototypes and spatially decoding only sampled frames.
aP3ipuT59Y.evidence: Evaluated on MOVi-C, MOVi-E, and YouTube-VIS against SlotContrast and SRL across inference chunking protocols and per-update cost benchmarks on precomputed features.
aP3ipuT59Y.claimed_gains: CoSlot achieves video FG-ARI scores of 72.2 on MOVi-C and 81.9 on MOVi-E without slot contrastive or explicit slot regularization losses, with lower cost per optimizer update on precomputed features than SlotContrast and SRL.
aP3ipuT59Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating multi-frame binding context from dense spatial decoding via compact shared-prototype reconstruction and sampled spatial decoding is a clear, computationally appealing design.
aP3ipuT59Y.main_concern: Empirical quality trails SlotContrast and SRL across most metrics and datasets, particularly on real-world YouTube-VIS and mBO, leaving the quality-to-training-cost trade-off unconvincing.

3aXNcppOVP.one_liner: Two-stage contrastive alignment pretrains co-aligned high-rank multimodal Earth observation targets before training geospatial location encoders.
3aXNcppOVP.problem: Lipschitz location encoders have intrinsic output dimension at most 2 and suffer spectral collapse under joint training, while frozen unimodal image targets do not extend directly to incompatible multimodal observations.
3aXNcppOVP.method: LoCA uses a two-stage contrastive alignment pipeline designed to provide co-aligned, high-effective-rank supervision targets. Stage 1 jointly contrastively pretrains Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 encoders, and Stage 2 trains the location encoder against those frozen multimodal encoders.
3aXNcppOVP.key_idea: Contrastively co-align multimodal Earth observation encoders first to form a high-rank frozen target onto which a coordinate location encoder can fold.
3aXNcppOVP.evidence: Supported by a Lipschitz intrinsic-dimension proof for contrastive location encoders and empirical evaluations across 17 tasks spanning ecological, environmental, and land-cover modeling.
3aXNcppOVP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clarity and simplicity of the two-stage frozen-target training pipeline, the distinction between intrinsic dimension and covariance rank, and the broad evaluation across 17 tasks.
3aXNcppOVP.main_concern: Reviewers question the technical originality of the Lipschitz dimensionality theorem and frozen-target framing relative to prior work, alongside missing comparisons with recent multimodal location encoders.

DsDsfb70CC.one_liner: Jointly learns contextual language latents and a diffusion generator from random initialization without pretrained language components.
DsDsfb70CC.problem: Latent language diffusion typically depends on pretrained language features or a separate representation-learning stage.
DsDsfb70CC.method: LDLM-s trains a language-modeling autoencoder and diffusion denoiser end to end from scratch. Language-modeling supervision shapes the latent space while selective diffusion gradients let the encoder and generator co-adapt.
DsDsfb70CC.key_idea: Jointly shape a contextual autoencoder latent space and its diffusion denoiser using language-modeling supervision and diffusion-objective co-adaptation.
DsDsfb70CC.evidence: OpenWebText experiments compare quality-diversity and repetition behavior with diffusion baselines and LDLM, including low-entropy and near-real-text-entropy regimes.
DsDsfb70CC.claimed_gains: LDLM-s extends the tradeoff toward lower generative perplexity while using roughly 5× fewer training tokens than LDLM, which reaches higher-diversity operating points.
DsDsfb70CC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning contextual latents without pretrained language models is interesting and that comparable performance with fewer tokens is promising.
DsDsfb70CC.main_concern: Reviewers question the claimed quality-diversity improvement and note missing component ablations, MAUVE comparisons, and training-cost measurements.

2jc1vCiFPB.one_liner: Branches alternative association decisions under a frozen policy to distill future identity preferences into online trackers.
2jc1vCiFPB.problem: Learning from future consequences of current data-association decisions in online multi-object tracking is difficult because alternative choices alter surviving tracks and identity bindings.
2jc1vCiFPB.method: Track-OPD branches alternative associations from the same tracker state under shared future observations and a frozen policy, evaluates them on the same annotated objects, and constructs a local teacher that redistributes probability between the ground-truth reference and poorer alternatives.
2jc1vCiFPB.key_idea: Rolls out alternative association branches from a shared tracker state under a frozen policy to build a local teacher from future identity outcomes.
2jc1vCiFPB.evidence: Experiments adapting MeMOTR, SambaMOTR, and MOTIP on DanceTrack and SportsMOT, plus bidirectional transfer and fixed ground-truth preference controls.
2jc1vCiFPB.claimed_gains: Improves HOTA over continued training by 1.03–1.36 points across evaluated trackers, and gains 0.543 HOTA and 1.184 AssA over unit ground-truth preferences at 4,000 updates.
2jc1vCiFPB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an important long-horizon supervision problem in online tracking with an innovative framework and consistent empirical gains.
2jc1vCiFPB.main_concern: Training-time computational overhead is not analyzed, and one reviewer flagged a serious discrepancy in Table 6 claiming motion prediction experiments on MOTIP.

5u9RCxIgSd.one_liner: Audits knowledge-graph foundation models under answer-preserving schema rewrites and applies purity-filtered structural normalization.
5u9RCxIgSd.problem: Knowledge-graph foundation models may not give invariant answers when the same facts are encoded via direct edges versus reified nodes.
5u9RCxIgSd.method: The authors formalize answer-preserving schema rewrites while holding queries, candidates, and facts fixed, and evaluate purity-filtered structural normalization and consistency training to restore predictions.
5u9RCxIgSd.key_idea: Evaluates KGFMs under controlled answer-preserving schema rewrites and applies purity-filtered structural normalization to recover canonical graph motifs.
5u9RCxIgSd.evidence: Evaluations across seven benchmark graphs, three message-passing backbones (including ULTRA, MOTIF, TRIX), and WD50K in Wikidata statement-node encoding.
5u9RCxIgSd.claimed_gains: Reification reduces ULTRA's MRR by 17–55% on six of seven graphs and changes top-1 answers on 60–90% of queries; normalization achieves exact edge-level recovery on 44 of 148 rewritten instances.
5u9RCxIgSd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly distinguishes link invariance from schema invariance and provides a well-controlled protocol showing severe sensitivity to schema rewrites.
5u9RCxIgSd.main_concern: The structural normalizer's guarantees mismatch its implementation on shared-relation motifs, and normalization is only lightly evaluated across backbones beyond ULTRA.

eRlGRLYmM2.one_liner: Replaces per-task Gaussian processes in latent-space molecular Bayesian optimization with pretrained prior-data fitted networks.
eRlGRLYmM2.problem: Latent-space Bayesian optimization fits a surrogate anew from limited observations for each objective without transferring experience across tasks.
eRlGRLYmM2.method: PILBO pairs a pretrained tabular in-context predictor (prior-data fitted network, PFN) operating directly on molecular representations with latent-space molecular generation. The authors also test continued pretraining (CPT) on synthetic molecular objectives constructed as BO episodes.
eRlGRLYmM2.key_idea: Uses an off-the-shelf pretrained prior-data fitted network on molecular representations as a zero-shot in-context surrogate for decoupled latent-space Bayesian optimization.
eRlGRLYmM2.evidence: Evaluated on eight GuacaMol multi-property molecular optimization objectives against Inv-BO and COWBOYS, plus ablations on representations and continued pretraining.
eRlGRLYmM2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pretrained PFNs serve as strong, practically useful surrogates in decoupled latent-space Bayesian optimization and outperform top baselines.
eRlGRLYmM2.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over combining PFNs with COWBOYS, modest gains from CPT, and a lack of analysis showing PFNs actually reduce initial GP surrogate error.

375leMFsja.one_liner: Generates paired original and drifted databases to benchmark LLM SQL query repair by execution-based semantic equivalence.
375leMFsja.problem: Schema changes silently break or alter production SQL queries, yet existing benchmarks do not guarantee drift impact, data migration semantics, or execution-based equivalence.
375leMFsja.method: DriftBench procedurally generates paired original and drifted databases, migrates data via canonical plans, and derives oracle SQL repairs. A candidate LLM repair is judged correct only if it reproduces the pre-drift result set on the instance database and ten independently seeded databases.
375leMFsja.key_idea: Procedurally pairs original and migrated databases with oracle queries to score LLM SQL repairs by exact result-set equivalence across eleven seeded databases.
375leMFsja.evidence: Evaluates eleven LLMs and deterministic/heuristic baselines on a 2,000-instance rename benchmark, structural drift, column semantic transforms, and 300 real mined instances.
375leMFsja.claimed_gains: On the 2,000-instance rename benchmark, eleven LLMs reach 88.8–94.9% semantic equivalence versus 13.7% for a fuzzy heuristic; on column transforms, six of nine systems execute 98–100% of the time while only two exceed 20% equivalence.
375leMFsja.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that execution-based evaluation of SQL repair under schema drift addresses a real, costly production problem.
375leMFsja.main_concern: Reviewers note that result-set matching can still accept semantically wrong repairs on specific databases, and that stronger models already saturate the main rename and split tasks (>90–100%).

kj9XVoC49T.one_liner: Proves retaining one noisy reference bit beats optimal adaptive sampling restricted to paired difference comparisons.
kj9XVoC49T.problem: Paired audits that store only whether two noisy query responses differ rather than raw responses incur an unknown statistical cost that adaptive sampling might or might not recover.
kj9XVoC49T.method: The authors analyze estimating an unknown bit from noisy control and informative queries under a fixed budget when only pairwise equality comparisons are observed. They derive exact minimax risks and error exponents for fixed designs, an all-horizon optimal adaptive policy, and a reconstruction scheme retaining one noisy reference bit.
kj9XVoC49T.key_idea: Derives exact finite-budget minimax risks for paired-only binary audits and shows one retained noisy reference bit reconstructs all raw responses on a connected graph.
kj9XVoC49T.evidence: Supported by exact finite-N minimax and all-horizon optimality theorems without empirical experiments.
kj9XVoC49T.claimed_gains: Fixed paired-only designs achieve half the raw-record error decay rate, while retaining one noisy reference bit in a connected comparison graph attains the full raw-record rate.
kj9XVoC49T.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers praise the exact finite-horizon minimax closure and clean graph-quotient lemmas, though a third found the paper unreadable.
kj9XVoC49T.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the lack of connection or empirical validation against the motivating LLM vulnerability audits and note obscure, non-self-contained writing.

gZLHfSkiuA.one_liner: Replaces audio VAE decoder backpropagation during few-step guidance with a single precomputed mean Jacobian.
gZLHfSkiuA.problem: Training-free guidance for latent audio diffusion requires expensive backpropagation through the VAE decoder at every sampling step or training gradient-imitating latent heads.
gZLHfSkiuA.method: Mean-Jacobian guidance (MaJa) precomputes a single decoder Jacobian averaged over a handful of training states and reuses it across all states, prompts, and steps. Paired with an attribute-value prediction head, it removes the decoder from the sampling loop.
gZLHfSkiuA.key_idea: Averages the audio VAE decoder Jacobian over a few training states once and reuses that fixed matrix with an attribute head to eliminate decoder backpropagation.
gZLHfSkiuA.evidence: Evaluated across two open-weight audio generators and five DSP/audio attributes against decoder backpropagation and cosine-0.99 gradient-imitating heads.
gZLHfSkiuA.claimed_gains: MaJa matches or outperforms differentiating the decoder in 14 of 16 settings across two generators and five attributes, and reduces target error by 31% on average relative to learned latent guidance heads.
gZLHfSkiuA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that MaJa is a clean, straightforward, well-tested technique for eliminating costly VAE decoder backpropagation in audio guidance.
gZLHfSkiuA.main_concern: Reviewers note the evaluation is limited to five low-level loudness/EQ DSP attributes (where post-processing gets zero error) and criticize terse writing that pushes key details to the appendix.

7Ku9SqUwde.one_liner: Reallocates training-time optimization weights across five clinical error categories for radiology report generation using online mirror ascent.
7Ku9SqUwde.problem: Sequence-level radiology report generation methods weight clinical discrepancy types statically, failing to adapt as the generator's error profile evolves during training.
7Ku9SqUwde.method: ACRA maps generated and reference reports into a structured finding space to track greedy-decoding risks across five discrepancy categories, then applies prior-regularized online mirror ascent to weight a risk-aware self-critical training objective.
7Ku9SqUwde.key_idea: Uses prior-regularized online mirror ascent over EMA-tracked discrepancy risks to dynamically weight a self-critical training objective removed at inference.
7Ku9SqUwde.evidence: Experiments on MIMIC-CXR and IU-Xray datasets using an R2GenCMN backbone.
7Ku9SqUwde.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adapting optimization priorities to evolving clinical error types during training is well-motivated and cleanly formulated.
7Ku9SqUwde.main_concern: Empirical validation is limited to an outdated R2GenCMN backbone, lacks comparisons against tuned nonuniform static weights, and achieves relatively low absolute clinical F1 scores.

T5ZQveFFN1.one_liner: Selects privileged critic inputs online using a paired confidence bound on actor update noise in asymmetric actor-critic RL.
T5ZQveFFN1.problem: Offline selection of privileged critic features based on return-prediction accuracy can actually increase actor gradient variance because a better value predictor is not always a better baseline.
T5ZQveFFN1.method: The authors decompose privileged signal contributions into action-independent offsets and action-dependent contrasts, and propose Online Informed Actor-Critic (OIAC) to re-select critic inputs via a paired confidence bound on update noise with cross-fitted Monte Carlo updates.
T5ZQveFFN1.key_idea: Re-selects privileged critic inputs online via paired confidence bounds on actor update variance rather than offline return-prediction accuracy.
T5ZQveFFN1.evidence: Theoretical variance decomposition and tabular simulation experiments comparing four selection rules.
T5ZQveFFN1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the theoretical decomposition distinguishing return-prediction accuracy from actor update variance.
T5ZQveFFN1.main_concern: OIAC offers unclear practical advantage over a history-only critic or variance-optimal baseline, and evaluation is confined to tabular tasks with readability issues noted.

uKAmcZXgJi.one_liner: Trains a half-edge graph policy via backward-walked behavior cloning and PPO to reach Gauss-Bonnet vertex-regularity bounds in quad meshing.
uKAmcZXgJi.problem: Generating coarse, all-quadrilateral block decompositions that achieve the provable Gauss-Bonnet minimum vertex irregularity is a sparse-reward combinatorial problem.
uKAmcZXgJi.method: The agent applies local edits directly on a mesh's half-edge data structure using a policy network with mesh-connectivity convolutions, enabling generalization to larger domains. It overcomes sparse rewards via behavior cloning on trivial optimal meshes walked backward into demonstrations, followed by PPO fine-tuning targeting the irregularity floor.
uKAmcZXgJi.key_idea: Pretrains a half-edge convolutional policy via behavior cloning on backward-walked optimal meshes, then refines with PPO toward the Gauss-Bonnet irregularity floor.
uKAmcZXgJi.evidence: Evaluated on 96 held-out domains and 64 double-size domains against seven Gmsh configurations, plus a BC-only vs. BC+PPO training ablation.
uKAmcZXgJi.claimed_gains: On 96 held-out domains, the agent produces all-quadrilateral meshes on all 96, usable ones on 95.7 on average, and reaches the regularity bound on 90, versus 0 for Gmsh at matched element counts.
uKAmcZXgJi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the agent strongly outperforms Gmsh on regularity and that the BC-to-PPO ablation clearly demonstrates the value of RL.
uKAmcZXgJi.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient differentiation from Narayanan et al. (arXiv:2309.06484) and lack of downstream PDE or finite-element validation.

j7OOgZTIUj.one_liner: Analyzes long-horizon meta-optimization in deep matrix factorization to explain why terminal loss induces Muon-like spectral flattening.
j7OOgZTIUj.problem: Why spectral flattening of gradient updates (as in Muon) improves optimization and whether it emerges naturally from long-horizon objectives remains unclear.
j7OOgZTIUj.method: Studies meta-optimization of update transformations evaluated by future terminal loss in deep matrix factorization, deriving an exact identity pricing update energy by how long gradient descent leaves it in place.
j7OOgZTIUj.key_idea: Evaluates update preconditioners via a long-horizon terminal-loss meta-objective, showing persistent low-curvature directions force flatter singular spectra.
j7OOgZTIUj.evidence: Theoretical analysis on solvable decoupled/deep matrix factorization models alongside empirical meta-optimization experiments on deep linear networks and MLPs.
j7OOgZTIUj.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers appreciate the meta-optimization perspective explaining why spectral flattening emerges for long horizons.
j7OOgZTIUj.main_concern: Reviewers note a mismatch between step-wise Frobenius normalization in experiments and initialization-only normalization in theory, plus MLP results favoring direction over spectrum.

lmSw3cM1yQ.one_liner: Factorizes audio-visual representations into shared, modality-specific, and domain-nuisance subspaces to steer deepfake detection away from audio shortcuts.
lmSw3cM1yQ.problem: Cross-domain audio-visual deepfake detectors ignore visual manipulation cues and rely on spurious audio shortcuts that loss-level regularization fails to remove.
lmSw3cM1yQ.method: TRIROUTE applies a three-way representation factorization separating shared content, modality-specific task-relevant features, and residual domain-dominant signals, allowing inference-time intervention by zeroing nuisance or misleading factors without retraining.
lmSw3cM1yQ.key_idea: Enforces a three-way subspace factorization so visual manipulation routes can be isolated and steered at inference time by zeroing nuisance factors.
lmSw3cM1yQ.evidence: Evaluated on cross-domain audio-visual deepfake detection (including FakeVideo-RealAudio splits) with head ablations, input masking, and subspace probes.
lmSw3cM1yQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets an important audio-shortcut failure mode (FakeVideo-RealAudio) with thorough probing analyses.
lmSw3cM1yQ.main_concern: Performance is fragile to the nuisance speaker-hash partition (FV-RA AUC drops from 0.838 to 0.694 under random regrouping), and direct comparisons to FCD and visual-only baselines are missing.

tkkPa8544w.one_liner: Infers multidimensional Bayesian AI performance-cost frontiers from aggregate benchmark and leaderboard records.
tkkPa8544w.problem: Scalar benchmark rankings hide measurement uncertainty, task heterogeneity, and cost-performance tradeoffs across model-harness configurations.
tkkPa8544w.method: The paper models each evaluated configuration as a composite of model, harness, and inference effort, recovers anonymous task-success histograms from aggregate pass@k totals via a unitriangular system for Beta-Binomial uncertainty, and estimates multidimensional frontiers.
tkkPa8544w.key_idea: Recovers task-success histograms from aggregate pass@k scores to fit Beta-Binomial multidimensional Bayesian frontiers across models, harnesses, and costs.
tkkPa8544w.evidence: Evaluated on Terminal-Bench v4, tau^3-bench, external leaderboard records, and a paired trial-level panel with prior-sensitivity checks.
tkkPa8544w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value recovering task-success histograms from public aggregates to model Beta-Binomial uncertainty and task heterogeneity.
tkkPa8544w.main_concern: Frontier probabilities are sensitive to omitted cost/duration noise and trial correlations, lifecycle switching relies on unvalidated assumed priors, and frontier-membership calibration is untested.

hRFNpEkRF7.one_liner: Residual-transformed supervision and subspace-structured gradient noise jointly suppress backdoor formation in vertical federated learning.
hRFNpEkRF7.problem: Malicious passive VFL parties can exploit exposed supervision and gradient feedback to implant backdoors during collaborative optimization.
hRFNpEkRF7.method: Residual-Transformed Alignment changes passive-party targets so they learn information missing from the active party's prediction. Subspace-Structured Gradient Perturbation injects structure-aware noise into gradient subspaces to suppress class-discriminative attack signals.
hRFNpEkRF7.key_idea: The defense reshapes both residual supervision and gradient-subspace feedback, reducing signals available for backdoor learning rather than detecting attacks afterward.
hRFNpEkRF7.evidence: Experiments span multiple datasets, party configurations, data modalities, and attack settings, with clean-task performance measured alongside attack success.
hRFNpEkRF7.claimed_gains: ResSub reduces average attack success rates from 89.7% to 8.3% while maintaining competitive clean-task performance.
hRFNpEkRF7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preventing backdoor formation through supervision and gradient feedback is well motivated and supported by broad dataset experiments.
hRFNpEkRF7.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite evaluation against only two non-adaptive attacks and missing VFL-specific defense baselines, leaving adaptive robustness unresolved.

7TaBtjkOfN.one_liner: Grows zero-initialized parallel attention and FFN pathways per Transformer layer to isolate and transfer LLM RL updates.
7TaBtjkOfN.problem: Reinforcement learning for LLM reasoning is computationally expensive, and standard weight updates cannot be cleanly extracted and reused across target models.
7TaBtjkOfN.method: GrowRL freezes the pretrained Transformer backbone and attaches an independent causal attention branch and FFN branch with zero-initialized output projections at each layer. RL trains only these added pathways, which can then be transferred and adapted sequentially onto structurally compatible frozen target models.
7TaBtjkOfN.key_idea: Isolates RL updates inside zero-initialized parallel attention and FFN branches per layer so learned reasoning pathways transfer directly across compatible backbones.
7TaBtjkOfN.evidence: Evaluated across five backbones (including Qwen2.5 and Llama 3.2) on mathematical reasoning, out-of-distribution tasks, and three transfer directions against full-parameter RL, LoRA, DoRA, and Parallel Adapter.
7TaBtjkOfN.claimed_gains: Learned pathways yield immediate gains across all three transfer directions, with strong performance after 10 target-side updates.
7TaBtjkOfN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the architecture simple, well-written, and effective at making RL computation structurally reusable with better same-family transfer than LoRA.
7TaBtjkOfN.main_concern: Structural compatibility is left undefined and transfer is only tested across three matched-scale same-family pairs, while compute overhead, parameter counts, variance metrics, and code are missing.

njZJbvqUdG.one_liner: Reuses prior cross-encoder scores via prefix-rescoring policies to update top-k rankings after query revisions.
njZJbvqUdG.problem: Search pipelines re-run expensive cross-encoder reranking over the entire candidate pool after every query revision even when relative rankings largely persist.
njZJbvqUdG.method: Differential neural reranking exploits shared score shifts and cutoff-concentrated membership changes using two prefix-rescoring policies: a zero-refit two-parameter crossing-risk model and a shift-plus-conformal-margin prefix extender. It also defines an exact hindsight oracle to bound minimal recomputation.
njZJbvqUdG.key_idea: Decomposes revision score changes into shared shifts and local cutoff crossings to rescore only a dynamically sized top prefix.
njZJbvqUdG.evidence: Analyzed across eight retrieval domains, two reranker architectures, 273 successive session revisions, and 250 held-out TopiOCQA conversations.
njZJbvqUdG.claimed_gains: The hindsight oracle needs 2.65 of 64 fresh evaluations for top-10 recovery; fixed-pool reranking achieves ~6x GPU speedup at >0.99 nDCG@10 fidelity; TopiOCQA saves 17.9% of warm-turn evaluations at 0.9997 fidelity.
njZJbvqUdG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the minimum-recomputation oracle framing, the shared-versus-residual score shift analysis, and the realistic multi-turn evaluation.
njZJbvqUdG.main_concern: Practical gains rely on concatenated-history retrieval that maximizes candidate overlap at the expense of gold-passage retrieval quality, and the live experiment omits the crossing-risk and conformal-calibration policies.

D1NiQGqc9D.one_liner: Measures input-conditioned functional substitutability between Transformer components to analyze scaling redundancy and guide dynamic routing.
D1NiQGqc9D.problem: Component importance and representational similarity are indirect proxies that miss whether intermediate neural components actually induce interchangeable downstream behavior.
D1NiQGqc9D.method: The authors introduce Conditional Functional Substitutability (CFS) to quantify how closely substituting one intermediate state with another preserves downstream responses on a given input. They use CFS to study functional reorganization across Transformer scales and train CFS predictors for dynamic head routing.
D1NiQGqc9D.key_idea: Defines redundancy directly by input-conditioned downstream response similarity under component substitution, then predicts CFS for adaptive head selection.
D1NiQGqc9D.evidence: Evaluated across modalities and Transformer families, controlled GPT-2 capacity scaling experiments, correlation comparisons against Taylor importance, and dynamic head-routing experiments.
D1NiQGqc9D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers view CFS as a clear, intuitively motivated direct measure of functional redundancy that outperforms Taylor importance in dynamic head routing.
D1NiQGqc9D.main_concern: Experiments are narrow in scope (focused on attention heads, GPT-2 scaling, and single-layer routing), some metrics do not control for candidate-head count, and the link to scaling laws lacks quantitative validation.

zJFVyMspIF.one_liner: Learns a task-agnostic speed prior from handheld and teleoperated demonstrations to retime robot trajectories before VLA fine-tuning and optimal-control execution.
zJFVyMspIF.problem: Teleoperated robot demonstrations encode slow, operator-specific pacing that policies inherit, while prior retiming methods require per-task fitting, annotations, or fixed rate heuristics.
zJFVyMspIF.method: The authors train a single speed prior conditioned on task instructions, motion paths, and wrist images over robot teleoperation (DROID) and faster handheld (FastUMI) demonstrations to predict an execution-speed distribution. Selecting a quantile defines a non-uniform clock to retime robot demonstrations before VLA fine-tuning, paired with a real-time optimal-control tracking layer at execution.
zJFVyMspIF.key_idea: Predicts a task- and path-conditioned speed distribution from handheld and robot demonstrations to retime teleoperated trajectories uniformly across tasks before VLA fine-tuning.
zJFVyMspIF.evidence: Evaluated on 120 RoboLab tasks and 3 real-robot tasks, comparing against uniform acceleration and filtered-BC controls.
zJFVyMspIF.claimed_gains: On 120 RoboLab tasks, fine-tuned policies succeed more often and move with up to half the jerk compared with baseline policies.
zJFVyMspIF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that transferring non-uniform execution pace from handheld demonstrations to teleoperated data via a learned speed prior is intuitive and practically engineered.
zJFVyMspIF.main_concern: Reviewers note that cross-domain transfer from FastUMI is not isolated from a DROID-only higher-quantile prior, the speed prior's gains are confounded with the new optimal controller, and comparisons omit strong adaptive retiming baselines (e.g., DemoSpeedup, SAIL, ISR).

ynBuiaNHoQ.one_liner: Learns a zero-inflated hurdle structural graph, embeds it in hyperbolic space, and generates sample-adaptive gates for Kolmogorov-Arnold Network sequence prediction.
ynBuiaNHoQ.problem: Standard sequence models treat exact zeros in zero-inflated time series as low continuous values rather than distinct inactivity events, distorting learned temporal dependencies.
ynBuiaNHoQ.method: CAST fits a hurdle-style zero-inflation-aware structural equation model (ZI-SEM) to jointly learn activity occurrence and conditional magnitude as a temporally ordered dependency graph. It embeds this graph in hyperbolic space to produce hierarchy-aware positional representations that drive sample-adaptive gates modulating nonlinear basis activations in a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN).
ynBuiaNHoQ.key_idea: Extracts a hurdle-style zero-inflated temporal dependency graph, embeds it in hyperbolic space, and turns the embeddings into adaptive gates inside a KAN predictor.
ynBuiaNHoQ.evidence: Supported by theoretical analyses of the two-part likelihood and hyperbolic/gating properties, controlled synthetic studies, and real-world retail/e-commerce benchmarks with ablations.
ynBuiaNHoQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating zero inactivity from active magnitude is well motivated and that CAST achieves strong F1 with ablations showing each component contributes.
ynBuiaNHoQ.main_concern: Reviewers cite excessive architectural complexity with scattered theory, a fabricated citation (attributing Judea Pearl's book to Didelez and Pigeot), unvalidated real-world graph recovery, and evaluation restricted to retail/e-commerce data.

1OUCvCCvvC.one_liner: Predicts which variable assignments from cheap early MILP solver incumbents persist in full-budget solutions to guide variable fixing.
1OUCvCCvvC.problem: Learning-based MILP accelerators struggle to predict complete solutions from static instance graphs alone and ignore structural information revealed early in the solver's search.
1OUCvCCvvC.method: EnCore shifts the GNN prediction target from full variable assignments to early-to-final consistency: given cheap early-stage solver solutions, it predicts which variable values will survive into full-budget solutions. At inference, consistency predictions are ensembled across multiple early-stage solutions to guide downstream variable fixing and search.
1OUCvCCvvC.key_idea: Trains a GNN to predict whether each variable's assignment in cheap early MILP solver incumbents will persist in the final solution, ensembling predictions to fix consistent variables.
1OUCvCCvvC.evidence: Evaluated on four MILP benchmarks integrated into three downstream frameworks under Gurobi (including solver transfer and runtime-budgeted ablations), plus two theoretical results.
1OUCvCCvvC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that leveraging early feasible solver incumbents to predict assignment persistence is intuitive, preserves feasibility, and yields consistent gains across MILP benchmarks.
1OUCvCCvvC.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty relative to incumbent-conditioned learned large-neighborhood search and missing simple heuristic baselines such as fixing variables that remain stable across early solutions.

mhT9x4MJZ0.one_liner: Allocates neural-operator latent points via an importance-balanced KD-tree to match local spatial complexity on million-point CFD meshes.
mhT9x4MJZ0.problem: Local-aggregation neural operators scale to million-point industrial CFD meshes but underperform global pointwise models because uniform latent allocation mismatches spatially varying sharp flow features.
mhT9x4MJZ0.method: The Importance-Balanced Operator (IBO) integrates a spatial importance measure reflecting geometry and flow complexity into a KD-tree partitioning algorithm to distribute latent tokens non-uniformly across the domain. This concentrates latent resolution where reconstruction is harder while maintaining low computational cost.
mhT9x4MJZ0.key_idea: Uses an importance-weighted KD-tree to allocate neural-operator latent points proportionally to local spatial geometry and flow complexity.
mhT9x4MJZ0.evidence: Supported by a decoder resolution error bound proof and experiments on industrial-scale 3D CFD benchmarks including DrivAerML, UrbanWind, and DriverNetML.
mhT9x4MJZ0.claimed_gains: Matches or outperforms compared models on industrial-scale CFD with approximately 5–40x fewer FLOPs (from TL;DR; abstract states no specific numbers).
mhT9x4MJZ0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formalizing spatially adaptive latent allocation is theoretically sensible and achieves strong empirical scaling at much lower compute cost.
mhT9x4MJZ0.main_concern: Reviewers view KD-tree spatial partitioning as incremental over prior adaptive-mesh/tree neural operators (e.g., AMR-Transformer, AB-UPT), note unisolated encoding/decoding changes, and highlight weaker surface-pressure predictions on DriverNetML.

0ZJBm1Las0.one_liner: Replaces pointwise surrogate regression in offline model-based optimization with distribution-aware pairwise ranking focused on high-quality versus remaining designs.
0ZJBm1Las0.problem: Offline model-based optimization surrogates trained by pointwise regression align only indirectly with the ranking comparisons needed to select near-optimal candidates during optimization.
0ZJBm1Las0.method: The authors separate optimizer reachability from surrogate selection, defining an optimization-oriented ranking risk between eps-optimal and non-eps-optimal designs and bounding selection error via training-to-target pair mismatch. Guided by this bound, Distribution-Aware Ranking (DAR) concentrates pairwise ranking training on high-quality-versus-remaining candidate pairs from the offline dataset.
0ZJBm1Las0.key_idea: Trains an offline MBO surrogate with pairwise ranking concentrated on high-quality-versus-remaining pairs to reduce mismatch with optimizer-induced selection comparisons.
0ZJBm1Las0.evidence: Supported by selection-error theoretical bounds and 10-seed experiments on Branin and five Design-Bench continuous and discrete tasks.
0ZJBm1Las0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating reachability from selection clearly motivates ranking surrogates and that DAR is simple and competitive on Design-Bench.
0ZJBm1Las0.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments do not isolate DAR's pair sampling from the hinge loss (lacking a global-sampling hinge ablation), omit strong baselines like RaM-ListNet, and may fail when the offline dataset lacks truly high-performing regions.

krpMZaRhZk.one_liner: Constructs exact score-companion pairs and minimum forecast-budget bounds for anytime-valid calibration attribution from finite forecast trajectory samples.
krpMZaRhZk.problem: Fitting a population-defined calibration projection on a finite sample of forecast trajectories biases the audit target, producing nonzero residual means even when the true component is zero.
krpMZaRhZk.method: PATHTAIL constructs a score and companion statistic whose expectations preserve the population residual component and tolerance from finite forecast samples, supporting anytime-valid sequential auditing. On finite domains, it characterizes the minimum fixed forecast budget needed for bounded exact scores and compares score constructions such as pooled-count estimators.
krpMZaRhZk.key_idea: Designs unbiased score-companion statistics from finite forecast paths that preserve population projection targets and enable anytime-valid sequential calibration audits.
krpMZaRhZk.evidence: Supported by an exact eight-path counterexample, finite-domain budget theorems, paired detection studies, and controlled feedback from four native forecasting models across eight data sources.
krpMZaRhZk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the finite-sample projection bias problem is well defined and mathematically sound, with an interesting score-companion construction.
krpMZaRhZk.main_concern: Reviewers criticize poor writing organization and heavy unintroduced jargon, and question practical utility since main evaluations use controlled synthetic outcomes rather than real held-out time series.

AAuBpcpEei.one_liner: Generates query-specific financial evaluation rubrics via expert-guided writer-reviewer agent loops and a reusable Task Bank.
