AAuBpcpEei.problem: Expert-authored finance benchmarks rely on static per-item rubrics that are expensive to update as financial facts change and cannot reflect institution-specific standards.
AAuBpcpEei.method: FinAutoRubric lets experts encode reusable principles and criteria in a Task Bank as prompts and code-enforced rules. Long-horizon writer-reviewer agent loops research, verify expected values as of an information cutoff, and escalate unresolved failures to humans, alongside releasing a 100-query benchmark across 78 tasks.
AAuBpcpEei.key_idea: Separates reusable expert evaluation rules and a Task Bank from long-horizon writer-reviewer agent loops that synthesize, verify, and human-escalate query-specific financial rubrics.
AAuBpcpEei.evidence: Evaluated on three expert-authored finance benchmarks with ablations, human grading agreement, blind analyst preference studies, and the released 100-query FinAutoRubric Benchmark.
AAuBpcpEei.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating reusable expert principles from automated query-level rubric synthesis addresses a practical challenge in financial agent evaluation, backed by analyst preference checks.
AAuBpcpEei.main_concern: Reviewers note missing controlled tests of dynamic cutoff or rule updates, unpenalized extraneous criteria in coverage metrics, documented rubric errors missed by review, and no cost/efficiency comparison.

F6D9zHCQIa.one_liner: Stress-tests LLM reasoning across complexity depth, answer-preserving perturbations, faithfulness, and novelty, analyzing depth-perturbation interactions.
F6D9zHCQIa.problem: High accuracy on static math and logic benchmarks does not verify whether LLM reasoning holds under deeper problem complexity or controlled surface perturbations.
F6D9zHCQIa.method: The authors evaluate 14 model configurations (including reasoning-disabled counterparts) across two generated task families up to depth n=12 and five benchmark references, separating answer-preserving from answer-changing transformations and modeling how perturbation costs compound with depth.
F6D9zHCQIa.key_idea: Separates answer-preserving from answer-changing perturbations across a controlled depth ladder to measure how perturbation fragility compounds with complexity and diverges from static benchmark accuracy.
F6D9zHCQIa.evidence: Evaluates 14 configurations over 10 model checkpoints on two generated task families (depth up to n=12) and five benchmark references including MATH-500.
F6D9zHCQIa.claimed_gains: Benchmark accuracy and stress behavior correlate overall (Spearman rho = 0.92), but configurations within 5 percentage points on MATH-500 differ by up to 23.8 points in answer-preserving robustness gap and disagree on 8 of 91 pairs.
F6D9zHCQIa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating answer-preserving from answer-changing perturbations and running extensive, transparent cross-depth stress experiments is methodologically solid.
F6D9zHCQIa.main_concern: Reviewers find the divergence from benchmark accuracy weak once distinct checkpoints or unsaturated benchmarks are considered (rho = 0.98), note narrow synthetic scope, and report difficult-to-read writing.

DHLdCi7Gir.one_liner: Guides partially observable multi-goal LLM agents with an online Simple Temporal Network that monitors deadlines and triggers refinement.
DHLdCi7Gir.problem: Existing LLM planning methods assume fully known static tasks and fail when agents must actively explore under partial observability while meeting hard multi-goal deadlines.
DHLdCi7Gir.method: The authors maintain an online partial Simple Temporal Network (STN) built from the agent's current knowledge base to constrain action selection and balance exploration against deadlines. When a temporal violation occurs, semantic feedback prompts iterative action refinement, evaluated on a new DeadlineBench benchmark.
DHLdCi7Gir.key_idea: Maintains an online partial Simple Temporal Network over discovered facts to constrain LLM action selection under deadlines and feed violation diagnostics back into prompt refinement.
DHLdCi7Gir.evidence: Evaluated on DeadlineBench (38 household and 33 laboratory tasks) against planning baselines across first-trial and repeated-trial runs with ablations.
DHLdCi7Gir.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coupling costly information acquisition with concurrent hard deadlines in DeadlineBench and separating temporal constraints via an online STN is a meaningful problem formulation.
DHLdCi7Gir.main_concern: All three reviewers flag method-dependent benchmark selection in Appendix C (adding tasks specifically because baselines failed or the proposed method succeeded), compromising evaluation independence.

opfEbCgG4c.one_liner: Inserts a geometric spatial concept bottleneck between robot perception backbones and action heads to enable human or VLM interventions.
opfEbCgG4c.problem: Learned generalist and specialist robot policies operate as black boxes that humans or vision-language models cannot easily interpret or steer at inference time.
opfEbCgG4c.method: The authors define spatial concepts as scene-geometry relationships between task entities and the robot—instantiated as navigation costmaps and manipulation relative-position offsets—placed between a perception-planning backbone and an action head. Humans or VLMs can inspect and modify these intermediate concepts to correct or steer actions.
opfEbCgG4c.key_idea: Compresses scene perception into explicit geometric spatial concepts (costmaps and relative offsets) between backbone and action head so humans or VLMs can directly intervene at test time.
opfEbCgG4c.evidence: Evaluated in closed-loop navigation and robot manipulation settings across bottleneck training variants and test-time human/VLM intervention experiments.
opfEbCgG4c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly presented and demonstrates that compact geometric spatial representations can support test-time policy steering and correction.
opfEbCgG4c.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over standard concept bottleneck models, an accuracy drop with predicted concepts (75.0% vs 83.8% direct baseline), and unclear definitions of navigation distances and VLM intervention mapping.

5ZSj1eQRxX.one_liner: Updates online conformal prediction thresholds using an epsilon-insensitive hybrid quantile loss with residual mapping and momentum smoothing.
5ZSj1eQRxX.problem: Online conformal inference methods relying on standard quantile loss react passively to non-stationary distribution shifts, producing conservative intervals or slow adaptation.
5ZSj1eQRxX.method: The authors introduce an epsilon-insensitive Hybrid Quantile (epsilon-HQ) loss adding a bounded quadratic component with gain balancing, and build a Dual-Calibrated Online Conformal Inference framework (epsilon-HQ-DCOCI). It pairs adaptive residual mapping and insensitive-zone tuning with momentum-based smoothing of historical subgradient directions.
5ZSj1eQRxX.key_idea: Replaces standard quantile loss with a gain-balanced epsilon-insensitive hybrid quadratic-linear loss paired with adaptive residual mapping and momentum-smoothed subgradient updates for conformal thresholds.
5ZSj1eQRxX.evidence: Provides Lipschitz, generalized weak pseudo-convexity, and dynamic regret proofs, plus experiments on financial time series and medical image classification.
5ZSj1eQRxX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modifying the update loss with a bounded quadratic component and modular dual calibration is a reasonable, well-motivated direction for non-stationary online conformal inference.
5ZSj1eQRxX.main_concern: All three reviewers identify a flaw in the asymptotic coverage proof: Corollary 5.4 claims vanishing average regret from O(sqrt(T(1+V_T))) while only assuming V_T = O(T), alongside modest empirical gains.

eDXifjr6Fv.one_liner: Models conversational emotion trajectories with a Neural Jump ODE decomposing continuous dynamics into gated self-cause and interlocutor-cause drivers.
eDXifjr6Fv.problem: Conversational emotion recognition models treat emotion as discrete per-utterance labels and rely on separate post-hoc modules to detect shifts and attribute causes.
eDXifjr6Fv.method: PSYCHE represents each speaker's emotion as a latent continuous trajectory governed by a Neural Jump ODE, where speech acts trigger discrete jumps and Causal Source Decomposition (CSD) splits inter-utterance drift into a decaying self-cause driver and an attention-based interlocutor-cause driver fused by a per-dimension gate.
eDXifjr6Fv.key_idea: Governs speaker emotion with a Neural Jump ODE whose drift decomposes via a learned gate into state-dependent self-decay and interlocutor-attended triggers, computing attribution during the forward pass.
eDXifjr6Fv.evidence: Evaluated on IEMOCAP and MELD with retrained baselines, component ablations, and dynamics analyses.
eDXifjr6Fv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reframing conversational emotion as a continuous jump-ODE trajectory with explicit separation of self-history and interlocutor influence is intuitive and supported by CSD ablations.
eDXifjr6Fv.main_concern: Reviewers note that the gate is trained with LLM-derived attribution priors and shift losses rather than establishing true causal identification, and flag selective reporting of LLM baselines on MELD plus extra commonsense features.

q2wSXSleTh.one_liner: Augments safe multi-agent locomotion policies with periodic LLM-generated strategy embeddings fused via a learned gating module.
q2wSXSleTh.problem: Safety-constrained multi-agent continuous control often relies on complex Lagrangian cost critics and dual variables to balance task reward against safety budgets.
q2wSXSleTh.method: The framework periodically queries an LLM during training with compact textual summaries of robot state and safety statistics to generate cooperative strategies. Strategy embeddings are injected into agent observations through a learned gate under CTDE with fixed reward penalization, leaving low-level MARL optimizers unchanged.
q2wSXSleTh.key_idea: Periodically queries an LLM with textual state-safety summaries to produce cooperative strategy embeddings that condition CTDE agent observations through a learned gate alongside fixed reward penalties.
q2wSXSleTh.evidence: Evaluated across six Safe Multi-Agent MuJoCo locomotion tasks (including LLM-HAPPO) with ablations on reward shaping, rule-based generators, gating, encoders, and query frequency.
q2wSXSleTh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the modular, lightweight framework is clearly presented and includes broad ablations showing improved reward-safety trade-offs across Safe Multi-Agent MuJoCo tasks.
q2wSXSleTh.main_concern: Reviewers highlight heavy reliance on manually engineered, task-specific state-to-text interpreters and prompts, limited methodological novelty, and inconclusive isolation of LLM reasoning from handcrafted rules.

RLBEeYYv3n.one_liner: Measures generalization versus canary extraction orderings in masked diffusion language models across repetition and dataset-size regimes.
RLBEeYYv3n.problem: While continuous diffusion work suggests population generalization precedes memorization, it is unknown whether this ordering universally holds in masked diffusion language models.
RLBEeYYv3n.method: The authors train masked diffusion language models on controlled Markov and hierarchical-grammar populations mixed with trained canaries and never-trained controls, comparing Bayes-referenced population denoising against canary extraction across repetition and dataset-size interventions.
RLBEeYYv3n.key_idea: Uses Bayes-referenced population denoising and controlled canary-repetition decoupling in synthetic masked diffusion language models to map when training-record extraction precedes or follows population learning.
RLBEeYYv3n.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic Markov and hierarchical-grammar populations across three paired seeds, decoupling canary probability and mixture fraction, plus pretrained-model checks.
RLBEeYYv3n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled experimental design (paired seeds, censoring, and frequency decoupling) cleanly demonstrates that the learning-versus-extraction ordering reverses with canary repetition.
RLBEeYYv3n.main_concern: Reviewers argue that memorizing out-of-distribution random canaries under higher repetition is an expected exposure-allocation effect rather than background-sample memorization, and that the theoretical results are elementary.

Gzw6oYmjqR.one_liner: Localizes unseen P&ID equipment from unresolved graph connectivity residuals for roster-grounded VLM verification and constrained graph completion.
Gzw6oYmjqR.problem: Digitizing piping and instrumentation diagrams fails on project-specific unseen devices lacking visual training examples and risks inserting structurally invalid process-graph connections.
Gzw6oYmjqR.method: TopoPID uses unresolved topology residuals in a partial process graph to localize candidate missing equipment, constrains VLM semantic verification with drawing-specific equipment rosters and geometric refinement, and updates the graph only under explicit structural conditions.
Gzw6oYmjqR.key_idea: Uses unresolved connectivity residuals in a partial P&ID graph to spatially localize unseen devices for roster-grounded VLM verification and deterministic constraint-checked graph updates.
Gzw6oYmjqR.evidence: Evaluated on held-out industrial P&IDs and zero-adaptation transfer to the public PID2Graph OPEN100 dataset against whole-page VLM and endpoint-cropping baselines.
Gzw6oYmjqR.claimed_gains: Improves identity-aware equipment recognition F1 from 80.38% to 93.77% over endpoint-guided cropping (and from 19.44% per TL;DR) and achieves 94.77% incidence F1 on correctly recognized equipment.
Gzw6oYmjqR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that turning unresolved graph topology into a spatial search prior while separating VLM recognition from deterministic graph updates is practical and yields strong recognition gains.
Gzw6oYmjqR.main_concern: Reviewers note that graph completion itself is not directly evaluated via edge insertion/deletion accuracy or pre-completion baselines, component ablations are incomplete, and the system mainly integrates existing tools.

ID2blmagnA.one_liner: Bootstraps full action-chunk Q-values from partial executions by combining observed prefix rewards with estimated unexecuted-suffix values.
ID2blmagnA.problem: Adaptive action-chunking RL executes only a prefix of each generated chunk before replanning, leaving full-chunk value critics without direct learning targets for the unexecuted suffix.
ID2blmagnA.method: Partial-Execution Q-Chunking (PEQC) retains generated action chunks during offline-to-online RL and constructs full-chunk Q-learning targets by combining observed rewards from the executed prefix with the estimated value of the original unexecuted suffix.
ID2blmagnA.key_idea: Constructs full-chunk Q-value backup targets from partial executions by summing observed prefix rewards with the bootstrapped value of the retained unexecuted action suffix.
ID2blmagnA.evidence: Evaluated on OGBench manipulation and navigation tasks (including AntMaze, Cube Triple, AntSoccer, HumanoidMaze) with paired significance tests, confidence intervals, and backup/collector ablations.
ID2blmagnA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mismatch between full-chunk evaluation and prefix execution is clearly formulated, and the experimental reporting with paired tests, ablations, and negative results is thorough.
ID2blmagnA.main_concern: Reviewers note that a simpler executed-prefix backup recovers most of the gain without evaluating the unused suffix, results depend heavily on the data collector, and performance lags or ties baselines on several tasks.

Bm4kHyVJWt.one_liner: Quantizes recursive Transformers using a shared low-bit backbone plus terminal-sensitivity-allocated sparse INT2 temporal overlays.
Bm4kHyVJWt.problem: Recursive Transformers reuse shared weights across loops, causing uniform local quantization errors to propagate asymmetrically and degrade final predictions.
Bm4kHyVJWt.method: TEMPO keeps a shared low-bit weight backbone and adds sparse INT2 residual planes modulated by compact temporal codes on selected tiles. It ranks corrections by terminal sensitivity—how loop-specific perturbations affect final output—and allocates extra bits globally to minimize expected distortion.
Bm4kHyVJWt.key_idea: Augments a shared low-bit recursive weight backbone with temporally coded sparse INT2 residual planes selected via loop-to-output terminal sensitivity under a global bit budget.
Bm4kHyVJWt.evidence: Evaluated on the Ouro recursive Transformer family (Ouro-1.4B and 2.6B) across perplexity and downstream benchmarks such as LAMBADA and MMLU.
Bm4kHyVJWt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well organized and cleanly models how shared-weight quantization errors have unequal terminal impact across recurrent loops without duplicating per-loop weights.
Bm4kHyVJWt.main_concern: Reviewers flag unmatched baseline comparisons (importing LoopQ numbers with different calibration data and group sizes), evaluation limited to one niche model family (Ouro), and no real wall-clock speedups due to bf16 materialization.

UJ5GHBg0oq.one_liner: Preserves high-resolution backbone features and performs content-normalized cross-temporal feedback inside the encoder trunk for remote sensing change detection.
UJ5GHBg0oq.problem: Pretrained vision backbones aggressively downsample spatial detail and conventional temporal fusion overfits scene-specific appearance cues in remote sensing change detection.
UJ5GHBg0oq.method: RIFT-CD uses a stride-2 high-resolution stem on a DINOv3 ConvNeXt-Large trunk, embeds cross-temporal feature interaction inside the encoder in a content-normalized relational space, and regularizes backbone adaptation to curb late-stage scene specialization.
UJ5GHBg0oq.key_idea: Integrate cross-temporal feature feedback directly into a high-resolution stride-2 encoder trunk using content-normalized relational features and drift regularization.
UJ5GHBg0oq.evidence: Evaluated across seven remote sensing change-detection benchmarks with factorial N x M x F ablations and synthetic radiometric/noise robustness tests.
UJ5GHBg0oq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the mechanism-oriented factorial ablation separating resolution, normalization, and temporal feedback, as well as transparent compute reporting across seven benchmarks.
UJ5GHBg0oq.main_concern: Reviewers point out confounded comparisons against frozen-backbone ChangeDINO, modest novelty combining existing ideas, and a 3.75x compute cost (399G vs. 106G ops) for a 0.32 F1 gain on LEVIR-CD.
